[191] Introduction and summary

[192] Continued strengthening and modernization Norway needs a defense to fulfill the fundamental and timeless responsibility of creating security for the state, the population and society

[193] The defense of Norway, and the design of Norwegian security and defense policy, has since the Second World War been based on the recognition that the security challenges facing Norway exceed what Norway will be able to muster in terms of capacity alone

[194] The comprehensive safeguarding of Norwegian security must, now as in the past, rest on both good utilization of society's overall ability to support defense capabilities and on collective and bilateral support and guarantees within the framework of NATO

[195] The defense of Norway is maintained through national efforts abroad and at home, and facilitation of allied efforts in Norway and in our surrounding areas

[196] Through this proposition, the government is facilitating the continued strengthening and modernization of the Armed Forces, building on the priorities and efforts in the previous long-term plan for the defense sector

[197] Norwegian security and defense policy must be based on the values and interests we want to secure

[198] These values ​​mean that Norway and our democracy can be developed within a framework of necessary freedom and independence, to ensure law and order, human rights and security

[199] Society must be able to safeguard and protect itself against serious threats to these values

[200] A credible defense is the state's most fundamental instrument for ensuring peace and stability

[201] Norway is facing a new security policy situation today and in the years ahead

[202] Not since the end of the Cold War have Norway and our allies faced such a range of simultaneous security challenges – against the state, society and the individual

[203] In the coming years, Norway must maneuver in a security policy landscape characterized by more direct competition and rivalry that can quickly develop into confrontation

[204] This challenges Norwegian and allied security

[205] Ongoing changes in our security policy environment concern all policy areas and the entire society

[206] Norway risks that its political room for action in several policy areas will be challenged against the backdrop of a deteriorating security situation

[207] Great power rivalry leads to increased instability and unpredictability

[208] International norms, rules of the game and institutions are breaking down

[209] The basis for constructive unity and cooperation within Europe and throughout the Euro-Atlantic area is under pressure

[210] At the same time, our vulnerability has increased, both for the Armed Forces' ability to operate and for society's overall resilience

[211] The increased use of complex instruments is a development that, among other things, results from the fact that modern societies and economies have become far more vulnerable

[212] It is therefore becoming more important for the defense of Norway to strengthen the ability to understand our surroundings and the ability to warn of threats across areas of society

[213] The global outbreak of COVID-19 appears in some areas to have exacerbated some of the negative developments in international security

[214] In addition to the pandemic's serious consequences for life and health, it has also challenged the security situation of many countries in a broader perspective

[215] Among other things, we have seen more restrictions on cross-border interaction and increased protectionism

[216] The negative security policy developments that the government pointed to in the previous long-term plan have increasingly become a reality for Norway, and we must take into account a further negative development of the security situation in our immediate areas

[217] A strong national defense is necessary to meet the challenges together with NATO and our allies

[218] Norway is today better equipped to safeguard our security interests compared to when the previous long-term plan was presented

[219] The government has taken important steps and turned around developments in the Armed Forces

[220] The armed forces are operating more and have a higher level of activity than in many years

[221] The initiatives that the government recommended and that the Storting endorsed in the previous plan are continuing and are now being realized

[222] At the same time, in this new long-term plan, we are laying the foundation for a further and gradual strengthening of defense capabilities through new and important initiatives over time

[223] It is expected that there will be more limited room for maneuver in the Norwegian economy in the years ahead

[224] The government nevertheless plans to use a large part of this room for manoeuvre to prioritize further strengthening of the Armed Forces

[225] Norway will spend significant resources investing in capabilities that NATO demands

[226] This will help increase national defense capabilities and strengthen NATO's collective defense

[227] Work will also continue on continuous improvement and efficiency in the sector

[228] The priorities in the defense area from the Granavolden platform have been followed up, and will be further followed up in this long-term plan

[229] In the further development of the structure of the Armed Forces, the government will first prioritize implementing decisions and measures from the previous long-term plan in this long-term plan period, as an absolutely necessary platform for further development of the Armed Forces

[230] During this period, the Armed Forces will continue the phasing in of new F-35 fighter jets

[231] In addition, the Armed Forces will begin the phasing in of new P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft and new coast guard vessels

[232] From 2021, priority will be given to gradually increasing staffing in the structure

[233] The initial service is being further developed, and the principles that have already been adopted for the Army are being applied to the entire Armed Forces

[234] Basic education is placed outside the operational departments

[235] Combined with increased staffing and new equipment, this will strengthen operational capability and increase the availability of the operational structure

[236] In addition, a number of measures will be taken that will overall reduce today's concurrency challenges, increase the ability to receive allied forces, and contribute to increasing the robustness and combat power of the Armed Forces

[237] The Government confirms an overall defense concept that clarifies that the defense of Norway consists of three interdependent elements

[238] our national capability, our collective capability within the framework of NATO's defense plans and our capability through bilateral support and reinforcement plans

[239] The complexity of the threat landscape also requires that military and civilian sides cooperate even more closely than before

[240] The defense of Norway is becoming more dependent on a modern total defense that helps support the national and allied defense efforts across the entire spectrum of crises, including on a daily basis

[241] The total defense concept involves utilizing the country's total resources in the best possible way

[242] The coronavirus pandemic has provided more experience in handling cross-sectoral situations

[243] The handling of the corona pandemic has shown that the total defense concept is also relevant in this type of crisis

[244] The pace of technological development is very rapid

[245] Long-range precision weapons that can reach the entire territory of Norway challenge warning times

[246] In addition, new weapons systems are being developed that reveal new types of vulnerabilities for Norway

[247] This is very expensive and demanding to handle

[248] Norway must be able to both defend itself against challenges arising from technology and be able to exploit the opportunities of technology in smart and effective ways

[249] The Armed Forces must modernize their capacities and increase their operational capabilities to be relevant in a new security policy situation

[250] Norway has a Defense Force that delivers high quality both abroad and at home

[251] The defense sector has dedicated and skilled employees and has a very good reputation in society

[252] Norwegian security is built together with others

[253] Norwegian security is safeguarded through efforts at home and abroad, primarily within the framework of NATO

[254] Collective defense, deterrence, and reassurance are once again central to the security policy agenda in Europe

[255] NATO and Norway's primary strategic goal is to avoid conflict

[256] Therefore, Norway must have a military force that is large enough to show that we can respond when we have to, and that enables allies to support us if this is required

[257] This need becomes more evident in a period when transatlantic relations are being put to multiple tests

[258] Unity, solidarity and agreement in NATO are of great importance for Norwegian security and freedom of action

[259] Norway will actively support unity in the alliance by taking our share of responsibility and leading where Norway has the conditions to do so

[260] The UN's Sustainable Development Goals see economic, social and environmental sustainability in context

[261] During the long-term plan period, the defense sector will strengthen its contribution to the achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goals by integrating the Sustainable Development Goals into the planning and management of the sector

[262] Balance between tasks with ambition, structure and finances

[263] To maintain economic sustainability in the development of the defense sector, there must be consistency between tasks with ambition, structure and finances

[264] The previous long-term plan established a good foundation for sustainability in the defense economy in a long-term perspective

[265] In the years before the previous long-term plan, lack of prioritization of maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks had led to a significant backlog

[266] The government has therefore prioritized significant funds in the period 2017–2020 to catch up on this backlog

[267] The maintenance level has also been increased to avoid new backlogs building up

[268] The worsening security situation means there is a need for reduced standby times

[269] To address this, the government has prioritized funds for increased activity and increased staffing for selected departments

[270] In addition, the government has prioritized investing in strategic capacities and we have initiated a necessary renewal of the equipment

[271] Through the significant investment in the Armed Forces in the previous long-term plan, the government embarked on extensive and long-term work to strengthen, modernize and further develop the defense sector

[272] The recommendations in this proposal assume that the adopted measures are continued

[273] This means that the implementation of the measures in the previous long-term plan also places significant financial constraints on future long-term plan periods

[274] Initiated investments must be completed

[275] The priority of reducing the backlog in maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks is maintained

[276] The establishment of new departments continues

[277] This long-term plan prioritizes ensuring that the planned measures achieve the necessary and expected effect

[278] This will help ensure that the further development of operational capability in the years ahead will be able to follow the security policy picture

[279] The long-term plans for the defense sector shall ensure long-term and sustainable development based on continuous and updated assessments and baseline analyses

[280] To ensure a good basis for choices and priorities, and to facilitate a broad and open defense debate, the government has, as part of the work on this plan, obtained several important inputs for the work

[281] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) prepared a research-based proposal, How to strengthen the defence of Norway, as the academic basis for the work on the new long-term plan

[282] The purpose of FFI's work was to show overall possibilities for the development of the Armed Forces

[283] The most central input to the new long-term plan is the Chief of Defence's Military Council (FMR

[284] the Chief of Defense prioritized improving the ability to solve the most important and demanding tasks, including strengthening preparedness and the ability to build up forces

[285] The Chief of Defence recommended a comprehensive strengthening of the Defence Forces, with an increase in volume, breadth and endurance, as well as an improvement in the ability to react

[286] The Chief of Defence also pointed to a significant need to reduce vulnerabilities in critical structural elements and to be able to contribute to NATO's collective defence and international efforts

[287] The work on the new long-term plan has been carried out in close coordination with the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's work on the upcoming white paper on "Social Security in an Uncertain World

[288] The increasing dependence between the Armed Forces and civilian sectors, and the increasing complexity of the threat landscape, require that civil-military cooperation be further developed holistically

[289] The White Paper will provide a more detailed account of the government's work on further developing social security work, and measures to strengthen resilience in civil society

[290] The Ministry of Defense established the Svendsen Committee in August

[291] Berit Svendsen, together with representatives from business, public agencies and the Armed Forces, was then tasked with providing input on how to use relevant lessons learned from private business and other public agencies to improve the Armed Forces' ability to recruit, retain, develop and terminate expertise, including developing the necessary diversity of expertise

[292] During the course of its work, the committee has provided input into the work on the new long-term plan with the Interim Report

[293] Pathways to increased diversity of expertise and implementation in the Armed Forces that place particular emphasis on diversity of expertise and technology

[294] Increased ability to combine humans and technology – paths towards a high-tech defense was submitted in June 2020, and was then sent for consultation

[295] The government has facilitated an open and broad debate on the further development of the defense sector

[296] Private individuals, associations, professional communities, municipalities, county authorities and other stakeholders were given the opportunity to provide their input into the long-term planning work

[297] Furthermore, the Minister of Defense invited municipalities and counties, the defense industry and other technology leaders, as well as personnel organizations, to dialogue meetings, which were also given the opportunity to provide their input

[298] Many written contributions to the work have been received from a wide range of contributors

[299] The development of the defense sector is a continuous process that aims to ensure that Norway has a defense that is best adapted to the prevailing security situation and at the same time takes into account new developments in a long-term perspective

[300] The Storting agreed to the recommendation

[301] P. no. 318, to the St.prop

[302] No. 48 (2007–

[303] – A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, towards a more continuous planning model for the defense sector

[304] This should ensure that development takes place to a greater extent through gradual adjustments within the framework of long-term goals, rather than through frequent and all-encompassing reforms

[305] The Storting will continue to be presented with an overall, holistic perspective on the development of the defense sector in each parliamentary term

[306] In the continuous long-term planning, greater emphasis is also placed on the ongoing development of the sector and on the fact that matters can be presented to the Storting when there is a need to inform the Storting or invite the Storting to make decisions on a matter

[307] Therefore, this long-term plan also outlines topics that the government intends to work on further and present to the Storting in the next long-term plan period

[308] Modern defense requires highly specialized expertise and advanced equipment, which has long lead times

[309] This requires a holistic and long-term perspective on the development of the defense sector

[310] The defense structure must be able to adapt to different development directions given changes in our surroundings

[311] Predictability around the overall political objectives and framework for the defense sector's activities is therefore crucial

[312] The work to develop and renew the defense sector extends through several parliamentary terms

[313] This long-term plan therefore provides a description of, and will guide, the development of the defense sector in both the short, medium and long term

[314] This is consistent with all long-term plans from recent times

[315] The government's financial commitment towards 2028 reflects the necessity of predictable and long-term frameworks, which, in light of security policy developments, must be in place in order to ensure appropriate further development of the Armed Forces' operational capabilities

[316] It is also essential that decisions are made in the correct order and that they are based on thorough assessments

[317] The main perspective in the plan is the upcoming four-year period

[318] The government also has a clear financial commitment to this long-term plan that also extends beyond the four-year period

[319] The government emphasizes that this strengthening should be gradual, and that it started with the significant economic boost that has been put in place during the period

[320] The purpose of the approach is to establish an even greater degree of predictability in continuous defense planning, and in the further development of the Armed Forces' operational capability

[321] The specific budget increase will be determined in each budget year

[322] The corona situation and any changes in the security policy situation are examples of why it is not appropriate to determine the specific allocation level in each individual budget year in a long-term plan with a long time horizon

[323] Security and defense policy frameworks and guidelines Norway's security policy environment and the framework conditions for Norwegian security are changing significantly

[324] Power shifts and great power rivalry, pressure against the rules-based world order, a more complex threat landscape, rapid technological development and more demanding military strategic development are all factors that affect Norwegian security

[325] The security situation has changed rapidly, and Norway must take into account that the negative development will continue

[326] For defense capabilities, this development is increasingly a question of national freedom of action, protection of Norwegian interests, and the ability to safeguard Norwegian influence, especially in areas close to Norway

[327] The defense of the country and the security of the population is one of the state's most important tasks

[328] Security policy developments mean that Norway will be able to have less influence over its own security

[329] Norway's strategic position in the North makes us particularly exposed to the consequences of a new security policy situation globally

[330] It is becoming more demanding to maintain the balance between credible deterrence and reassurance across the entire spectrum of crises and conflicts, at the same time as this balance is becoming increasingly important

[331] Norway must take greater responsibility in its own immediate areas, while at the same time becoming more dependent on allied cooperation

[332] In a new security policy situation, there is a need to clarify and strengthen the interdependent components of Norway's defense

[333] The Government has therefore, in this long-term plan, placed emphasis on updating the overall concept for the defense of Norway

[334] The defense of Norway takes place along three main lines: the national defense capability, the collective defense in NATO and, in particular, bilateral support and reinforcement from close allies

[335] Investment in defense capabilities should therefore support security and defense policy goals by providing impact along the three main lines in parallel

[336] The three main lines must be supported by a modern and prepared total defense that strengthens the nation's resilience and endurance, as well as reduces vulnerability to complex threats or other security-threatening activities

[337] This holistic approach to the defense of Norway forms the core of the defense concept

[338] The government will continue to modernize and strengthen the defense sector

[339] In addition, the government will emphasize the further development of total defense to ensure that society's overall resources are utilized to the best advantage for effectively handling challenges to both state and societal security

[340] The Government bases the further development of the defense sector and the implementation of defense policy on the following guiding principles: balance, realism, and a long-term perspective within a conceptual framework

[341] The tasks of the Armed Forces are to: Ensure credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defense Defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks and attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defense Avert and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including facilitating allied engagement Ensure a national basis for decision-making through surveillance and intelligence

[342] Asserted Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[343] Maintain the exercise of authority in defined areas Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace operations Contribute to international cooperation in the area of security and defense policy Contribute to the maintenance of societal security and other key societal tasks Key developments of importance for Norwegian security and defense capabilities

[344] Security and defense policy developments are influenced by political, technological, economic and demographic developments and by climate change

[345] This requires adaptability within the entire defense sector and affects long-term defense planning

[346] The long-term plan for the defense sector is being promoted at a demanding time for Norwegian security

[347] The coronavirus pandemic has reinforced several of the security policy developments we have seen in recent years

[348] Global crises of this nature can have profound consequences for Norwegian and allied security

[349] Developments in Russia, China, the United States and Europe, in transatlantic relations and in the security situation in the High North, are crucial for how the defense sector should be developed

[350] The security policy developments in Europe's neighboring areas are worrying and serious, with potentially major consequences for the individual area and for international peace and security

[351] We see that the great powers are modernizing their defenses on a full scale

[352] The strategic rivalry can play out below the threshold of armed conflict

[353] Technological advances are being offset and state security is being challenged more broadly through a more complex use of instruments

[354] The number of targeted threat incidents in the digital space against Norwegian authorities and businesses is increasing, and the threat from non-state actors against Norway and allies persists

[355] The lines between peace and conflict, and between conventional and irregular warfare, are becoming increasingly blurred

[356] The challenge is further complicated by the fact that the agreements and structures that regulate and limit the development and use of nuclear weapons are under pressure, and there are signs that the threshold for the use of weapons of mass destruction is being lowered

[357] Technological development is progressing very rapidly in many different areas, and as one of the world's most digitalized countries, this has significant implications for Norway

[358] High technological change rates and diffusion provide new opportunities, but at the same time challenge the current approach to structural development, procurement and management of systems

[359] Climate change may in the years ahead gain increased importance in security and defense policy and affect the ability of states to protect society and the population

[360] The defense sector will in future have a planned approach to climate and environmental measures

[361] Through such and other measures, the sector will also contribute to the fulfillment of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[362] Further development of the defense economy Maintaining a defense that can handle changing challenges in the current threat landscape requires a sustained willingness and ability to invest in the defense sector through adequate, stable and predictable financial frameworks

[363] To maintain economic sustainability in the development of the defense sector, there must be a balance between tasks of ambition, structure, and finances

[364] A number of conditions and factors have influenced and will influence the defense economy and the economic scope for action in the future, including currency exposure in the defense sector, defense-specific cost growth and requirements for efficiency improvements

[365] The defense sector must fulfill its mission within a comprehensive and responsible framework, in the short and long term

[366] A further economic boost for the defense sector is envisaged through a further strengthening of the defense budget, together with a number of resource-freeing measures

[367] Competence – a fundamental prerequisite for strengthening the Armed Forces

[368] The Government will further develop the personnel and competence area

[369] Personnel with the right expertise and the right composition must staff the sector's organization and capacities

[370] Further development and increased utilization of conscription, the reservist system, and cooperation arrangements with allies, business and other sectors are necessary areas of focus to increase access to relevant expertise

[371] The government is introducing an active reserve that can strengthen the staffing of the Armed Forces' departments if needed

[372] The Government will also facilitate a targeted effort for better civil-military cooperation within the personnel area

[373] The defense sector must be able to offer attractive and competitive career opportunities for both military and civilian personnel, and utilize a broad recruitment base and differentiated selection processes to facilitate the necessary diversity of expertise

[374] The further development of the education system, according to the principles laid down in the previous long-term plan, continues

[375] The Government will facilitate efforts to increase the quality, efficiency and relevance of vocational and functional education

[376] Veterans possess unique and crucial knowledge from military operations, which is an important foundation for the further development of the Armed Forces

[377] The government will continue veterans policy as a clear political priority

[378] Research and development (R&D), innovation and exploitation of technology

[379] It is important for the government to have good access to updated research-based knowledge and insight within the full range of defense and security policy issues

[380] R&D in the defense sector should complement civilian research and development activities

[381] The defense sector should make greater use of the national knowledge base and use research-based advice

[382] The defense sector has close cooperation with the national defense industry, which provides for the development of national defense industrial capabilities and knowledge base

[383] The defense sector's ability to benefit from the expertise of the business community beyond the traditional defense companies will be strengthened to make it easier for small and medium-sized companies to deliver to the Defense

[384] Defense sectors' collaboration with academia and Norwegian and international business is strengthened by further developing the arenas where the actors meet

[385] International cooperation on the development and procurement of solutions and materials is being further developed

[386] International knowledge sharing is a prerequisite for building strong national knowledge environments

[387] It is an ambition for Norway to become among the leading countries in Europe in innovation, and the focus on industry-oriented research and increased innovation capacity will continue

[388] Innovation activities and technology development in the defense sector should be viewed more holistically

[389] All agencies in the defense sector must, to a greater extent than today, facilitate innovation in their organizations

[390] The Government will further develop how various actors, schemes and financing mechanisms are organized to safeguard innovation, research and technological development in the defense sector

[391] Society's resilience and total defense

[392] The need to strengthen civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defense to meet an increasingly complex challenge picture is increasing

[393] The traditional distinction between state security and societal security is becoming less clear

[394] Civil-military cooperation must be developed holistically and continuously so that vulnerabilities across state and societal security are reduced

[395] The work on this long-term plan has been closely coordinated with the preparation of the societal security report, which provides a more detailed account of developments in civilian sectors

[396] The Government will strengthen the defense sector's ability to protect its assets

[397] The Armed Forces must both have the ability to handle complex threats to their own sector, and be able to contribute to broader management across sectors

[398] The Government will further develop the Intelligence Service's ability in peace, crisis and armed conflict to monitor, attribute, warn and actively counter digital threats before incidents occur

[399] The defense sector's ability to prevent, detect and handle threats in the digital space is being strengthened to protect the Defense's own operations

[400] The Government will also further develop and strengthen the expertise and professional environment surrounding strategic communication in the defense sector, and strengthen the environment for research and development in the field

[401] The overall national situational awareness is improved to be able to see threats and incidents in different sectors in context

[402] The Government will strengthen Norwegian authorities' situational awareness in space through cross-sectoral cooperation

[403] Better situational awareness in space will be sought in collaboration between the Armed Forces, civilian actors and close allies

[404] Total defence shall ensure the best possible utilization of society's resources in terms of prevention, emergency planning, crisis management and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum

[405] Civil-military cooperation and civil emergency preparedness work have also received greater attention within NATO in recent years

[406] Civilian support to military forces is crucial to defense capability, and work on contingency plans and measures to further ensure such support continues

[407] In addition, it is important to find solutions to include private businesses in planning for security crises and armed conflict

[408] One of the tasks of the Armed Forces is to contribute to safeguarding societal security and other key societal tasks

[409] Cooperation between the Armed Forces and the police has improved and will be further developed during this long-term plan period

[410] The Armed Forces can assist civil society at the request of civilian authorities when their resources are insufficient, or there are no relevant civilian resources

[411] This applies, for example, to natural disasters, epidemics, accidents and serious criminal acts such as terrorism

[412] An example of the Armed Forces' support for civil society is the assistance during the corona pandemic

[413] Preliminary consequences of the pandemic for the Armed Forces and for the Armed Forces' assistance to other societal preparedness are discussed

[414] security and defense cooperation

[415] The Government will further develop its efforts in the bilateral and multinational areas

[416] Norway prioritizes operational and security policy cooperation with selected allies that are relevant for allied and bilateral reinforcement of Norway in security policy crises and armed conflicts

[417] Cooperation with allies, including within the framework of NATO and other multinational forums, includes both presence in daily operations and the defense of Norway higher up the crisis spectrum

[418] Norway will continue to work for a global legal order through a strong UN

[419] Norway will contribute to constructive cooperation and seek solutions to the challenging conflicts that arise in the UN Security Council

[420] Norway will contribute to ensuring that UN peacekeeping operations remain a key instrument for international peace and security

[421] The Government continues its work to ensure NATO's relevance and credibility in the future, and supports constructive efficiency and reform measures

[422] Through growth in defense budgets during this period, acquisition of new modern capabilities and substantial contributions to NATO's readiness forces, force registers and operations, Norway continues to increase its contribution to burden sharing in the alliance

[423] Cooperation with close allies supports and complements NATO cooperation and thus contributes to increased allied defense capabilities

[424] The Government will work to strengthen security and defense policy cooperation with the EU, and contribute to the further development of dialogue and cooperation between the EU and NATO

[425] The Government will also continue active Nordic defense cooperation

[426] The allied dimension is crucial for the defense of Norway, and requires an active alliance policy

[427] The government wants an allied presence

[428] From a Norwegian perspective, it is important that the overall allied activities in the North in peacetime are clear, but at the same time predictable and coordinated so that the risk of unintentional misunderstandings and escalation is minimized, and that our strategic main line of balance between deterrence and reassurance is maintained

[429] At the same time, and as part of burden sharing, Norway must maintain the capacity to participate with force contributions in international operations and other international activities in close cooperation with close allies

[430] Further development of the structure of the Armed Forces The defence policy and the developments that define the security situation are the basis for the specific design of the structure of the Armed Forces

[431] The structure builds on the strategic choices made in the previous long-term plan period and the structure should be sustainable in both the short and long term

[432] The Government will develop the defense structure and facilitate further strengthening in upcoming long-term planning periods

[433] The development of the structure must also be seen in the context of our collective capability in NATO, as well as our bilateral reinforcement plans and relationships with close allies

[434] The Government first prioritizes strengthening the Armed Forces' response capability and endurance, through strengthened staffing and increased investment in emergency stocks beyond the level in the current long-term plan

[435] In the coming years, the Armed Forces will phase in a number of new capabilities and carry out several upgrades to existing capabilities to ensure technical and operational relevance

[436] This will ultimately increase the Armed Forces' operational capability and help close gaps within existing planning and NATO's capability goals for Norway

[437] This long-term plan calls for the government to begin work on phasing in several major material systems

[438] Among other things, the Bell 412 will be replaced by a new helicopter capacity that is better suited to special forces, and the Army will phase in new tanks from 2025 and long-range precision fire

[439] In the Air Force, the introduction of the new F-35 fighter jets and P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft will have top priority

[440] It is also planned to introduce four new submarines from the late 2020s

[441] Early in the coming period, a new surface structure will be investigated to replace today's surface combat vessels and ensure continued operational capability

[442] The Government does not intend to propose significant changes to the Armed Forces' base structure, beyond making adjustments within the current base structure to the structural changes that are recommended

[443] The long-term development of the base structure will, in addition to the daily need for force production and peacetime operations, facilitate national and allied defense plans

[444] It is necessary to further develop the Armed Forces' shooting and training ranges to meet new needs and requirements, and to better facilitate exercises and training between foreign and Norwegian departments

[445] Further development of the Armed Forces' structure requires a more flexible approach to the defense sector's property, buildings and structures (PBC) and the introduction of new cost-effective PBC solutions

[446] The Armed Forces' ability to provide logistical support must be strengthened to increase the responsiveness, availability, endurance and effectiveness of the rest of the Armed Forces' structure

[447] The Government is therefore continuing to strengthen the logistics field and establishing a national storage concept for storing combat-ready materiel

[448] Other agencies in the defense sector

[449] The Ministry of Defense has five subordinate agencies

[450] The Norwegian Armed Forces, Defence Materiel (FMA), Defence Construction (FB) and the Defence Research Institute (FFI) are both administratively and professionally subordinate to the Ministry of Defence

[451] The National Security Authority (NSM) is administratively subordinate to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and technically subordinate to both the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and the Ministry of Defence

[452] The Ministry of Defence therefore has the authority to instruct NSM in matters within the Ministry of Defence's area of responsibility

[453] Other agencies in the defense sector shall support the Armed Forces so that the Armed Forces' tasks can be solved in the most efficient manner possible and act as advisors to the Ministry of Defense within their own areas

[454] The agencies must continuously further develop cost-effective solutions across sectors so that the organization's quality and delivery capacity are further strengthened, and make adjustments to their own organization based on the sector's needs and developments

[455] The agencies shall also seek to develop existing and new collaborative relationships nationally and internationally within the guidelines of the Ministry of Defence

[456] The Armed Forces as a social actor

[457] The defense sector has a social responsibility for managing society's assets

[458] In the work to achieve the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, the goals that the sector should contribute to achieving are specified, along with a number of measures that build on the sustainability goals

[459] The defense sector also has a climate responsibility

[460] It is important to look more closely at how the sector can best reduce direct and indirect emissions, without compromising operational capability

[461] The defense sector is a significant steward of Norwegian cultural heritage and cultural environment, and produces a diversity of cultural experiences, and the government will seek to safeguard cultural activities in the defense sector

[462] The defense sector contributes significantly to value creation and jobs in society

[463] Significant funds are allocated each year to protect and safeguard Norway's security, interests and values

[464] The use of the funds has a major economic effect, not least in the places where the defense sector is located, but also elsewhere in the country

[465] The defense sector also provides support to a number of voluntary organizations and other non-governmental actors

[466] Implementation and management 2021–

[467] The defense sector's overall societal goals form the basis for the approach to exercising governance in the sector

[468] Based on the societal goal, there are three main areas that contribute to goal achievement

[469] The operational capability of the armed forces, the collective defense in NATO and the cooperation with close allies, supported by the total defense

[470] The management of the sector must be organized holistically by emphasizing the importance of the organizations collectively aligning themselves towards realizing the sector's social goals, and having good, effective and timely interaction based on the organizations' various missions, tasks, roles, authority and responsibilities

[471] Holistic, predictable and long-term management is of great importance for achieving desired effects and reaching the sector's goals

[472] Through clear goals and priorities, management should be simplified, streamlined and have a defined purpose

[473] The plan is to manage underlying businesses more generally and to follow up on results and effects to a greater extent, rather than resources and activities

[474] In order to achieve the highest possible utilization of resources, the Chief of Defence, in close collaboration with other heads of agencies, will be given greater room for manoeuvre to find the solutions that provide the best implementation

[475] The long-term development of the Norwegian defense sector must take into account that a high rate of change, increasing unpredictability and greater complexity will also characterize developments beyond the period 2021–

[476] Long-term development of a relevant defense requires a combination of predictability and flexibility

[477] It is crucial to create predictability around the overall political goals and framework for the business

[478] It takes time to further develop the Armed Forces' capabilities and capacities

[479] The Armed Forces shall prioritize capabilities that provide the greatest possible national operational capability, and which at the same time constitute relevant contributions to NATO's collective defense

[480] The necessary room for maneuver in the work on the long-term development of the defense sector requires continuous attention to improvement and efficiency

[481] It is also an important prerequisite for the realization of future long-term plans

[482] Increasing complexity in the threat landscape and a defense that is becoming more dependent on civilian support also require that civil-military cooperation be developed holistically

[483] Cooperation on the development of civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defense will be necessary to find good solutions for the future

[484] Part I Frames and guides

[485] Security and defense policy frameworks and guidelines

[486] The purpose of security and defense policy is to protect national security and enable Norway to respond to challenges across the entire crisis spectrum, from serious threats and incident management in peacetime, via security policy crises to armed conflict

[487] Norway's security policy environment is undergoing significant change

[488] Norway and allies face a more serious threat than when the previous long-term plan was prepared

[489] More instability and various forms of conflict cannot be ruled out in our part of the world in the coming years

[490] Challenges on the Western side can have a negative impact on the ability for cooperation, joint decisions and unity both within Europe and throughout the Euro-Atlantic area

[491] The challenges have become more demanding, while our vulnerability has increased within both state and societal security

[492] Norway and our allies are in a new security policy situation, where Norway's ability to maintain influence over its own security and promote and protect our values and interests is becoming more important, but also more demanding

[493] The security situation has changed rapidly, and Norway must take into account that the negative development will continue

[494] The implications for defense capability increasingly revolve around national freedom of action, protection of Norwegian interests, and the ability to maintain Norwegian influence, especially in Norwegian areas

[495] The government will continue to modernize and strengthen the defense sector

[496] In addition, the government will emphasize the further development of total defense to ensure that society's overall resources are utilized to the best advantage for the effective handling of challenges to both state and societal security

[497] Norwegian security and defense policy is based on a functioning international framework, a strong transatlantic security community through NATO and Norway's overall defense capability

[498] The state's most important task is to ensure the safety and security of its citizens

[499] Security and defense policy goals, the defense concept and the Armed Forces' tasks with associated ambitions constitute the overall security and defense policy framework and guidelines for the sector

[500] The framework and guidelines in this part of the proposal

[501] It is the basis for the specific design of other policy areas in the sector in general and for the structure, organization and activities of the Armed Forces in particular

[502] It is crucial to have a holistic and long-term perspective in order to create predictability for this development

[503] New security policy situation

[504] High rates of change, increasing unpredictability and greater complexity challenge our security, including in our own immediate areas

[505] Such a complex and confusing situation can lead to instability, misunderstandings and conflict

[506] This can be exacerbated by a lack of cooperation and dialogue

[507] States and institutions will seek to position themselves to become more resilient to this development

[508] Norwegian security is in a demanding period where great power rivalry, pressure on a rules-based world order, rapid technological development, complex threats and demanding military strategic development are central driving forces in a new security policy situation for Norway

[509] Power shift and great power rivalry

[510] There is currently an increasing great power rivalry with the United States, China and Russia as the main players

[511] Geopolitical rivalry is an element in this picture

[512] The global power shift towards Asia, and especially China, continues

[513] The dominant role of the West, led by the United States, is changing

[514] China represents a different outlook, different goals and values, and has clear and stated ambitions to achieve greater global influence

[515] Upheavals in the international balance of power have historically been associated with increased instability and the risk of conflict

[516] The open and growing rivalry between the United States and China already has extensive international consequences, and will be felt economically, technologically and in terms of security policy

[517] The global spread of the coronavirus and its handling seem so far to have intensified the contradictions between the great powers

[518] Although China and Russia are wary of each other, they are strengthening cooperation and coordination in some areas to better promote their respective interests to the outside world

[519] Both countries have an interest in strengthening their position internationally and to a greater extent challenging American and European interests

[520] This could also result in greater coordination between China and Russia in the UN Security Council, making it even more challenging than today to get the council to agree on decisions

[521] China and Russia are seeking in different ways to challenge existing norms and rules that have characterized the international order

[522] This leads to a less transparent and predictable world in which large players will take more control

[523] Multinational cooperation and dialogue are given less value and several policy areas may be influenced by strategic demonstrations of power on a scale we have not seen in many decades

[524] International politics is characterized to a greater extent than before by competition, rivalry and confrontation, where small states can more easily find themselves in a vulnerable situation

[525] There is a military and commercial technological race underway among the great powers

[526] This also includes the struggle for access to rare raw materials, knowledge and information

[527] America's military and technological dominance has been challenged, and in some areas probably equalized

[528] Both Russia and China currently possess extensive military capabilities that are capable of threatening the security and limiting the freedom of action of other countries

[529] These capabilities also reduce Western warning and protection capabilities and make defending Western territory very challenging

[530] Global stability in the coming years will depend largely on developments in relations between Western countries and China

[531] Alongside external challenges, the transatlantic community today faces increased internal challenges

[532] On both the European and American sides, we have seen the rise of populist and nationalist movements that are skeptical of globalization, free trade, immigration, and multilateralism

[533] In Europe, this also includes skepticism about the EU as a supranational project

[534] Contradictions between EU member states are increasing, and the ability to stick together and find common solutions is generally weakened

[535] The United Kingdom, one of Europe's great powers, has withdrawn from membership in the EU and will enter into a new relationship with the European community

[536] In sum, this poses a risk of increasing security policy divisions within Europe and across the Atlantic. The Western liberal world order, and the institutions established in the post-war period, have contributed to global stability and economic growth

[537] This was based on the idea that all parties should be able to promote their own interests through multinational frameworks and dialogue

[538] Central principles and values have been a market-based economy and free trade, individual rights and freedoms, a free press, the rule of law and democracy

[539] Internal and external factors are now challenging this liberal world order

[540] Trust and support for international law, international norms and institutions are weakening

[541] In certain areas, international law is under pressure, and Russian use of force in violation of international law has worsened security in Europe

[542] At the same time, China is challenging its neighbors and the possibility of free navigation in the South China Sea

[543] The great powers and the international community are increasingly at odds over which interests and common goods are most important, and whether and how these must be regulated and shared jointly

[544] In a world where power increasingly takes precedence over right, and where short-term interests gain increasing importance, the risk of confrontation and conflict increases. Technological development is now occurring at a scale, speed and potential impact on society that resembles a technological revolution

[545] The changes affect all policy areas and sectors, where the consequences for society and the defense sector are complex and challenging to predict

[546] Access to advanced, destructive technology has traditionally been reserved for major military powers

[547] This is no longer the case

[548] Innovation and distribution of technological capabilities and knowledge are accelerating

[549] Technology that can threaten the security of states is increasingly available to both state and non-state actors

[550] New technological breakthroughs provide increased range, greater destructive potential and better precision, against both military and civilian targets

[551] Digital space, space-based services and the electromagnetic spectrum enable actors to target others effectively, while reducing political risk

[552] Actors who aspire to have global security policy influence depend on innovative thinking about how to utilize military and commercial technology

[553] States that are able to quickly translate new technologies into military capabilities gain significant military advantages

[554] This includes areas such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, machine learning and big data processing, robotization and automation

[555] China and Russia in particular are competing with the United States and Western defense industries to realize such technological advantages first

[556] The pace of technological development is changing the framework conditions for security policy

[557] Previously, the dimensional Norwegian security challenge was clearly defined, and appeared primarily as a military problem

[558] Today, NATO countries, including Norway, must expect to be more frequently exposed to the complex use of instruments from both state and non-state actors

[559] Composite use of means involves the coordinated and coordinated use of different means and methods that support and reinforce each other in order to influence an adversary with hostile intent

[560] Information and communication technology facilitates the coordination of instruments in sophisticated and broad-based intelligence and influence campaigns

[561] Several actors are developing the ability to carry out complex, offensive network operations, where exploitation of third-party infrastructure, operations with sabotage purposes and encryption viruses are characteristic features

[562] Composite instruments are used across the entire spectrum of crises from peace to armed conflict

[563] Such use of instruments helps to make the distinction between societal and state security less clear

[564] The means used to achieve political goals can be diplomatic, informational, military, economic, intelligence and legal

[565] Disinformation, subversion, military signaling, acquisition of strategic resources, control over energy resources, and challenges to our legal order are examples of various forms of use of instruments that can represent such threats

[566] The threat of the use of military force creates room for maneuver for the use of other instruments and can contribute to making these more effective. The risk of interstate conflict is once again a current challenge in our part of the world

[567] The new security policy situation is characterized by variations of competition, rivalry and confrontation

[568] Misunderstandings and weak decision-making can increase the risk of conflict

[569] Our understanding of concepts such as peace, crisis and war is changing

[570] Conflict between states does not only occur in a limited geographical area, but can also unfold across domains

[571] Warfare has traditionally been associated with the domains of land, sea, and air

[572] Modern warfare more systematically exploits the traditional domains across, as well as outer space (the space domain), the digital space (the cyber domain), and the human domain (cognitive and social

[573] In addition, the electromagnetic spectrum creates an environment that connects the domains and enables communication, observation and identification

[574] The military dominance of the United States and the West is challenged, and we must deal with actors who have built up extensive offensive capabilities with long-range from mobile weapons systems

[575] The offensive capacity is protected by long-range defensive systems

[576] The development is serious and could promote incentives for the use of offensive weapons early in a conflict to achieve strategic advantages

[577] The importance of the initial phase of a conflict is increasing

[578] Large distances and long warning times have previously provided strategic and operational depth in conflict and warfare

[579] The depth has made it possible to distinguish between tactical, operational, strategic and political issues

[580] It has thus been possible to handle armed conflict for traditional command and decision-making structures

[581] Military strategic developments make handling crises and conflicts far more demanding

[582] Distance and time no longer provide the same advantages, but introduce new challenges for a defending party

[583] Modern society and modern military power depend on space-based infrastructure and services

[584] The importance of outer space and space activities is increasing

[585] At the same time, it is demanding to regulate space activities and the use of outer space

[586] The connection between space-based services, digital space and the use of our electromagnetic environment is becoming stronger

[587] New technologies are being developed that can impact space-based capabilities, such as communication and navigation systems

[588] The role of information in modern warfare is becoming increasingly comprehensive, integrated and sophisticated

[589] Norway is one of the world's most digitalized societies, where the population has a high level of trust in information

[590] At the same time, access to data itself has become an arena for competition and rivalry

[591] Modern technology makes it possible to blur the lines between a real and virtual world and between truth and falsehood

[592] Technological understanding and source criticism are necessary to understand an increasingly technologically advanced and interconnected world. A major challenge for Norway in a new security policy situation is the risk of marginalization of Norwegian security

[593] Great power rivalry and the increased strategic importance of the High North make Norway more exposed to changes in the security policy landscape

[594] Support for a rules-based world order and respect for the legitimate interests of smaller states cannot be taken for granted

[595] Where power precedes right, the risk increases that small states like Norway will come under cross-pressure or be placed in undesirable electoral situations

[596] A more demanding and volatile security policy landscape where change can and will occur quickly, and often dictated by a few dominant actors, is changing the framework conditions for Norwegian security

[597] It will require more from Norway to maintain influence in our immediate areas and safeguard our own security

[598] Investments in defense and security are necessary to maintain influence and continue to be able to make our own decisions about, and influence the decisions of others about, Norway's security

[599] Allied cohesion will remain under pressure

[600] Norway must continue to make significant efforts to strengthen the political community in NATO and the relationship with close allies. Deterrence and reassurance are becoming more important It is becoming more demanding to maintain the balance between credible deterrence and reassurance across the entire spectrum of crises and conflicts, at the same time as this balance is becoming increasingly important

[601] The costs of armed conflict appear increasingly unmanageable, especially for a small state

[602] Efforts to counteract conflict at all levels and with all means are becoming more important

[603] In this development, it is becoming increasingly crucial to understand what characterizes the normal state of Norwegian and allied security, and it is becoming more challenging to uncover deviations

[604] Many states experience minor non-military attacks on a daily basis, for example in the digital space, and influence from state and non-state actors

[605] However, this does not mean that classical deterrence and the importance of a credible defense become irrelevant

[606] The great powers are modernizing their defenses on a full scale

[607] The military capacity and deterrence of great powers provide greater room for maneuver to operate with higher risk in the gray area between peace and conflict

[608] There is a need to increase understanding of how the use of this scope for action impacts the national threat landscape, as well as to establish an adapted approach to and updated understanding of deterrence, in line with a new security policy situation

[609] Norwegian security and defense policy and the Armed Forces' efforts shall contribute to preventing armed conflict from occurring

[610] Norwegian security policy has long been characterized by a balanced approach that emphasizes both deterring hostile actors through our own military capabilities and our membership in NATO, and reassuring non-allies through dialogue, diplomacy and openness

[611] The policy has been designed at the intersection of the need for allied support, low tension towards the east, and domestic political considerations

[612] Central elements have been the base, nuclear and port of call policies, as well as the guidelines for foreign military activity in Norway

[613] This policy is being continued and has been important in our approach to Russia

[614] In the current security policy situation, continued deterrence and reassurance are therefore important for Norway

[615] It will be crucial to understand the actor picture in our immediate areas, which capacities and activities can challenge Norwegian security, and how we can help avoid misunderstandings and unintentional escalation

[616] Arms control has been an important confidence-building element in the European security architecture throughout the post-war period, not least in our immediate vicinity

[617] Unfortunately, the arms control regime is under pressure

[618] It is precisely in periods of heightened tension that mutually binding arms control agreements take on increased importance

[619] It is unfortunate that work on arms control has almost come to a standstill

[620] Renewed pressure on arms control is in Norwegian and European interests

[621] Norway has been a driving force in protecting and strengthening agreements that will contribute to openness and transparency about military activity and mechanisms to build trust and reduce uncertainty. State security is challenged more broadly State and non-state actors' use of complex instruments can impose several simultaneous dilemmas on a counterparty that potentially challenge state security

[622] A main challenge with this use of instruments is that it may ostensibly be aimed at societal security objectives, but in reality have serious implications for state security

[623] In this way, complex threats and the complex use of instruments help to make the distinction between societal and state security less clear

[624] Increasing complexity requires the ability to contribute to a higher degree of cross-sectoral situational awareness, and places increased demands on the defense sector's ability to solve its tasks and contribute to broad national coordination and sharing of responsibilities

[625] The threat landscape also places high demands on preventive security work both in the defense sector and in society at large

[626] The change in the use of instruments is faster and the escalation time from the use of one instrument to a comprehensive use of instruments that threatens state security can be very short

[627] This requires the ability to more quickly apply the nation's combined instruments so that effective countermeasures can meet developments in a timely manner. Norwegian security and defense policy aims to protect Norwegian sovereignty, territorial integrity, our democratic system of governance and our freedom of action against political, military and other pressure by contributing to

[628] – Protect Norway's population, territory, central societal functions and infrastructure against threats, attacks and attacks from both state and non-state actors – Prevent armed conflict and the emergence of threats to Norwegian and allied security – Promote peace, stability and further development of the international legal order – Defend Norway and allies against threats, attacks and attacks within an allied framework

[629] The security and defense policy objectives express what the government wants to achieve with security and defense policy, and in sum constitute the defense sector's societal goals

[630] Norway's security and defense policy goals have been adapted to the changed security policy situation

[631] The defense of the country and the security of the population is one of the state's most important tasks

[632] Traditionally, the task has been associated with the threat of the use of military force between states, or the use of violence by non-state actors against individuals or societal functions

[633] Today, we must also take into account to a greater extent that Norway is exposed to complex threats, where different instruments are used to support and reinforce each other

[634] This type of use of instruments is used to influence specific, time-limited activities or situations, or to have more long-term goals to undermine trust and weaken the state

[635] Through daily operations at home and abroad, the Armed Forces contribute to protecting the safety and welfare of the population, preventing armed conflict and threats to our and allied security, as well as promoting international peace, stability and further development of the international legal order

[636] This includes understanding our environment, warning and protecting against threats and attacks, as well as preventing and preventing threats from materializing both in our immediate areas and abroad. The Defence of Norway is based on a common understanding of what is to be defended and protected

[637] Norway is characterized by a geographical location in a strategically important area, our open economy, our position as a coastal state and manager of large marine resources, and extensive exports of oil and gas

[638] Norway is a high-tech society with a strong economy and global interests related to trade and industry, climate and environment, peace and reconciliation, human rights and humanitarian issues, and international security

[639] In a security policy context, Norway is a small state, and is dependent on functioning and as stable as possible relations between states

[640] Norway has a fundamental interest in protecting an international legal order and international agreements and norms where law takes precedence over power

[641] The connection to the Western security community remains crucial for the defense of Norway

[642] NATO membership and the collective security guarantee are the cornerstones of Norwegian security policy

[643] Likewise, a stable and predictable relationship with Russia is important for Norwegian security

[644] A long-term main objective will continue to be to balance deterrence and reassurance in our relationship with Russia, not least in the High North

[645] The defense of Norway depends on the total defense

[646] Total defense encompasses the mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society regarding prevention, emergency planning and operational matters

[647] Total defense includes relevant actors at all organizational levels, including voluntary organizations and private actors with responsibility for critical societal functions and critical infrastructure

[648] Norway's international law obligations establish an overarching legal framework for the sector's activities

[649] The use of military force in armed conflict is enshrined in international law

[650] The right to state self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, as referred to in Article 5 of the Atlantic Charter, are examples of such anchoring

[651] The same is true of Security Council resolutions that authorize the use of military force in accordance with Article 1 of the UN Charter

[652] The use of military force in armed conflicts is subject to the rules of international law on warfare

[653] The international law of war and national legislation establish the legal framework for the use of military force in armed conflict

[654] Norway's security policy room for manoeuvre is not a constant quantity

[655] In a world characterized by great power rivalry where the margins can be small from rivalry through confrontation and to conflict, there is a risk that small states like Norway will have less influence on their own security

[656] It may become more demanding to achieve security and defense policy goals

[657] The risk of coming under cross-pressure or being put in undesirable choice situations increases

[658] In an increasingly complex threat landscape, military means are used in combination with other means to test, destabilize and isolate Norway

[659] The use of complex instruments early in a crisis situation can reduce Norway's ability to defend itself with military means if the country is exposed to military aggression

[660] The High North's renewed and increased strategic importance for the great powers has direct consequences for Norway's security policy space

[661] The development emphasizes the importance of the long-term lines in Norwegian security and defense policy

[662] Investment in national defense and security is becoming increasingly important to maintain influence, credibility, and relevance to close allies

[663] Our national capacity and ability to follow and understand developments in our own immediate areas are of significant importance for maintaining Norwegian security policy room for manoeuvre. **2.4.2 Norway's strategic position in the North** The security situation in Norway's immediate areas is increasingly a strategic challenge, not only for Norway in isolation, but also for NATO and key allies

[664] Norwegian territory and our surrounding areas are gaining greater importance in light of Norway's geostrategic location

[665] NATO is strengthening the ability for collective defense in our immediate vicinity, and close allies want to play a more significant security policy role in the North

[666] Allied forces that are trained together with Norwegian units also increase the credibility of our own military capabilities

[667] Allied presence in daily life and Norway's ability to operate together with and receive allied reinforcements is becoming increasingly important for our deterrence and defense capabilities

[668] Norwegian and allied military presence in the north represents deterrent and reassuring considerations, where the goal of these instruments has continuously been to ensure stability and predictability vis-à-vis Russia

[669] The national ability for daily operations and presence is becoming increasingly important in ensuring Norwegian influence on the situation in our immediate areas

[670] A clear Norwegian presence helps to establish the most predictable and stable situation possible for military activity between neighboring countries in the region

[671] Box 2.1 The concept of security** Security policy shall safeguard state security

[672] That is, to safeguard security needs related to the existence, sovereignty and integrity of the state

[673] When state security is threatened, it can legitimize the use of many or all of the state's available resources

[674] State security encompasses not only the defense of Norwegian territory, but also Norwegian security interests and Norway's contribution to the security of NATO countries through the alliance's collective defense

[675] Resisting threats and challenges to state security is the primary responsibility of security and defense policy

[676] Increased global uncertainty and regional instability, also closer to Norway, mean that Norwegian security and defense policy must be geared to reducing the risk of armed conflict

[677] Societal security is about society's ability to protect itself against and handle events that threaten fundamental values and functions and put life and health at risk

[678] Such events can be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions

[679] The formulation of Norwegian security and defense policy is based on a security concept that encompasses an updated understanding of how state security, societal security, and individual security are interconnected in the defense of Norway

[680] It is also becoming clearer that state security can be affected by more and more sophisticated instruments, which have traditionally not been associated with a security risk to the state

[681] The use of complex instruments by state and non-state actors to exploit vulnerabilities, create unrest and achieve political or military goals makes it more difficult to define a threat

[682] This leads to the lines between the civilian and the military becoming more blurred, and emphasizes the need for close security and preparedness cooperation across sectors

[683] Maintaining state security is becoming more demanding and can be challenged through threats to individual and societal security

[684] Genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes can provide a basis for international action, including military action

[685] The security of the state and society is closely linked, both in daily life and during periods when the nation is exposed to demanding stresses

[686] Implications for the Armed Forces Norway must do more itself

[687] Norway's geostrategic location dictates that Norway must take significant responsibility on the alliance's northern flank, in the form of military presence in all domains, surveillance and intelligence

[688] At the same time, close cooperation with our closest allies, particularly the United States and the United Kingdom, remains important in these areas

[689] Norway, together with close allies, has taken a clear role in the North within the framework of NATO

[690] This is also NATO's and close allies' clear expectations of Norway

[691] Norwegian military presence in the High North is something Russia is both familiar with and accustomed to, and in which the United States and other close allies have confidence

[692] The activities of Norwegian military forces thus contribute to reassurance and stability and to ensuring Norwegian influence over our own security, while at the same time helping Norway remain a relevant partner for our close allies

[693] If Norway does not have a regular and predictable presence in the North, a space could arise that allies or other actors will fill

[694] Such a development could have negative consequences for stability, and Norway could lose influence over security policy developments in its own immediate areas

[695] Norway is becoming more dependent on allied cooperation

[696] Allied presence in daily life, as well as closer and more committed support and reinforcement across the entire spectrum of crises and conflicts from close allies, are becoming increasingly important prerequisites for safeguarding Norwegian security

[697] Bilateral and multinational cooperation structures are becoming more important than before

[698] It must be taken into account that local episodes and incidents can quickly escalate and spread to a larger geographical area and to multiple domains

[699] For example, Russia could activate an expansion of the bastion defenses and thus threaten both Norwegian territory and the transatlantic supply lines

[700] The defense of Norway is not based solely on NATO's response forces

[701] Norway must also rely on receiving reinforcements from close allies

[702] NATO's overall military response may take time and reinforcement of other areas may be prioritized over Norwegian territory

[703] In such a phase, operational cooperation with close allies, together with national efforts, is mandatory to defend Norway

[704] Therefore, a strengthened national defense with interoperability with close allies and the capacity for allied reception is crucial for Norwegian security. The Defense Concept describes the connection between the security and defense policy goals and the tasks of the Armed Forces with associated ambition

[705] The Norwegian Defence Force shall be organised so that national and allied efforts provide mutually reinforcing and simultaneous effects for Norwegian security

[706] It is the totality and balance between them that constitute Norway's overall defense capability

[707] The defense of Norway is a continuous effort on and outside Norwegian territory in peace, crisis and armed conflict

[708] This contributes to both deterrence and reassurance

[709] In a new security policy situation, there is a need to clarify and strengthen the interdependent components of Norway's defense

[710] The government has therefore placed emphasis in this long-term plan on updating the overall defense concept

[711] The defense of Norway takes place along three main lines: the national defense capability, the collective defense in NATO, and bilateral reinforcement plans with close allies

[712] Investment in defense capabilities should therefore support security and defense policy goals by providing impact along the three main lines in parallel

[713] The three main lines must be supported by a modern and prepared total defense that also strengthens the nation's resilience and endurance, as well as reduces vulnerability to complex threats or other security-threatening activities

[714] This holistic approach to the defense of Norway forms the core of the defense concept

[715] – Our national capability

[716] National defense capabilities are becoming more important and the need for national capabilities for operations and presence at home and abroad is increasing

[717] Increased military presence, including from allies, will demand more from the Armed Forces and there are increased expectations from allies of Norway's ability to handle and limit the consequences of unwanted incidents and episodes

[718] – Our collective capability in NATO

[719] Collective security through deterrence and defense is the alliance's most important mission

[720] Updated defense and reinforcement plans for the entire Alliance territory are the bedrock of our security guarantee

[721] All allies must contribute more to ensuring their own safety and that of others

[722] – Our bilateral plans for support and reinforcement from close allies

[723] Norway depends on operational cooperation and binding bilateral agreements to receive the necessary support in a crisis and in the event of armed conflict
