[724] Such agreements complement and strengthen national and collective capabilities

[725] The need for and interest in allied reinforcement and presence in Norway is increasing

[726] Such a conceptual approach facilitates a holistic understanding with a strong national dimension for the defense of Norway, and will help to counteract the marginalization of Norwegian influence over its own security and freedom of action

[727] A strong national defense will help strengthen our overall defense capability and thereby enable Norway to meet the full range of challenges

[728] The defense of Norway requires a strong national defense that facilitates and supports the allied dimension, while also having a credible ability to defend the country with national capabilities

[729] In the face of a new and more serious security policy situation, it is the sum of Norway's ability to influence and manage its own security, NATO's security guarantee and credible plans for early support from close allies that can deter attacks on Norwegian sovereignty, territorial integrity, our democratic governance and political freedom of action

[730] Combined with reassuring measures intended to demonstrate presence, maintain dialogue and cooperation, and avoid misunderstandings and unwanted escalation, the defense of Norway shall promote predictability and stability in our immediate vicinity

[731] If the combination of deterrence and reassurance does not prevent an actor from acting aggressively and carrying out attacks and attacks against Norway, it is the simultaneous combination of national capability, collective defense and the presence and reinforcement of close allies that constitutes our overall defense capability. [761] The primary task of the Armed Forces is to prevent threats and attacks from occurring, by contributing to credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defense

[762] The Norwegian Armed Forces, together with close allies and within the framework of NATO, shall contribute to effective deterrence so that potential aggressors refrain from political, military and other pressure to challenge or violate our sovereignty, territorial integrity, our democratic governance or political freedom of action

[763] Credible deterrence increases the cost of attacking to such an extent that a potential aggressor refrains from doing so

[764] Credible deterrence is ensured through a combination of robust internal capabilities, a modern total defense and an active alliance policy that is predictable, long-term and conflict-preventing

[765] NATO membership is the core of Norway's ability for credible deterrence

[766] NATO's primary purpose since the organization was founded has been to prevent armed conflict through a clear ability and willingness to defend the alliance by military means if necessary

[767] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall contribute to ensuring that NATO remains a credible alliance, also in our immediate vicinity

[768] This requires the ability to react immediately, effectively and with relevant means if Norway is exposed to pressure, threats or attacks, as well as the ability to cooperate with allied forces within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[769] The Armed Forces shall contribute to achieving NATO's capability goals and contribute to NATO's standing forces, readiness forces and staffing of headquarters

[770] Allied presence in the High North, as well as demonstrated ability to reinforce the defense of Norway through bilateral reinforcement agreements and NATO planning, contributes to effective deterrence

[771] Allied forces that train, exercise and operate together with Norwegian forces in Norway and the High North are a deterrent response to increased military activity in our immediate vicinity

[772] At the same time, robust national capabilities, presence and activity contribute to predictability and stability in our immediate areas, and reduce the risk of strategic misunderstandings and unintentional escalation

[773] The Armed Forces therefore have an important role in contributing to both deterrence and reassurance

[774] The ability to handle military challenges and other forms of pressure, nationally or together with allies, should help to prevent threats from arising

[775] The most demanding challenges involve the Armed Forces having the ability to conduct high-intensity combat operations over time in a national or allied joint operational framework

[776] The need for early warning requires that the Armed Forces must have the ability to be present to establish and maintain situational awareness throughout the Norwegian immediate area

[777] This contributes to a credible defense with a relevant response capability

[778] The Norwegian contribution to conflict prevention in our immediate areas is not created by individual capacities, but by the Armed Forces' combined resources

[779] The Armed Forces must therefore have the ability to coordinate efforts with several relevant capacities simultaneously

[780] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be able to protect its own capabilities, including its own military objects, its own military material and information. **Task

[915] In these areas, the Norwegian Armed Forces provide significant support to civil society on a daily basis. **2.7 Guiding principles for the development of the defence sector and the implementation of defence policy** Investment in defence and security is necessary for a small state's ability to resist pressure, attacks and attacks

[916] Norwegian independence, sovereignty and freedom of action must be defended even in peace

[917] Armed conflict and crisis in our part of the world are not unthinkable

[918] Warfare between technologically advanced and risk-averse actors could become more complex, massive, and destructive in its initial phase

[919] The most important thing Norway does is therefore to contribute to stability and to avoid armed conflict

[920] This makes deterrence the most important function for the Armed Forces

[921] In the new security policy situation, it is not enough to simply prepare the Armed Forces for armed conflict

[922] At the same time, the defense must be organized to be relevant, present and capable on a daily basis, so that Norway becomes less vulnerable to complex threats

[923] These functions are closely related

[924] In order to prevent armed conflict, the Armed Forces must be able to detect and handle incidents and events on a daily basis and to act quickly if a situation escalates and a crisis or armed conflict threatens

[925] The Government bases the further development of the defense sector on the following principles: balance, realism and long-termism within a conceptual framework

[926] There must still be a real balance between tasks, structure and finances

[927] The Armed Forces must be organized so that there is a connection between the tasks assigned to the Armed Forces by the Storting and the government, and the tasks that the Armed Forces can solve in practice

[928] To meet changing operational needs, resources are directed towards the most important tasks and capacities

[929] The Government continues to place emphasis on realistic calculations of cost developments for the capacities included in the recommended structure

[932] The development of the Armed Forces shall take place within a conceptual framework

[933] The update of the defense concept for the defense of Norway provides a clarification of the connection between the security and defense policy goals and the tasks of the Armed Forces with associated ambitions

[934] The concept provides a superstructure that will guide the further development of the Armed Forces

[935] Defense capability is made up of more than the sum of the capacities of the individual elements

[937] Realism in defense planning should be emphasized, so that operational capability, availability and preparedness are strengthened

[938] If, for economic reasons, large investments in military capabilities are not resourced sufficiently to be utilized optimally, this contributes to weakening the Norwegian Armed Forces' combat power, credibility and reputation

[939] Some of the biggest challenges for the Armed Forces have been related to operations, resulting in inadequate maintenance and emergency logistics, as well as lack of staffing, presence, training and exercises

[941] This remains an important measure for the Armed Forces to be able to carry out their assigned tasks

[942] The government will continue to emphasize the use of resources on staffing, maintenance, spare parts, emergency stocks and training of prioritized capacities

[943] Decisions must be substantiated in a long-term perspective

[946] The long-term cost picture must be carefully assessed in connection with large investments, and investment costs in a shorter perspective must be seen in the context of the gain in operational capability over time

[969] Norway's security policy environment

[970] Russia poses a greater security challenge for Norway and the Western security community than in decades

[971] The Putin regime's overall political goals are to maintain its own power and regime stability, secure influence and control in former Soviet states, and restore Russia's status as a great power in international politics

[972] The potential of Russian military power has changed significantly in just a few years

[973] Russia's behavior is increasingly assertive and risk-taking

[974] The willingness of Russian authorities to use a wide range of military and non-military means to achieve their goals has increased

[975] The negative democratic development within Russia, the conflict in Ukraine, Russian military involvement in Syria, military activities and initiatives on the African continent, as well as several cases of influence campaigns in and against Western countries illustrate the growing challenges

[976] Russia's violation of the INF Treaty (Intermediate Range Nuclear Forces Treaty), with subsequent termination of the agreement by the American and Russian sides, is also negative for stability in Europe

[977] These developments have contributed to increased antagonism and tension between Russia and Western countries, and have created greater uncertainty and concern about Russian intentions and actions

[978] The strengthening and modernization of military power in Russia continues

[979] Russia has demonstrated the ability to conduct complex joint operations and rapidly move military units over long distances

[980] Since 2008, the modernization of Russian offensive conventional weapons has moved towards much higher precision and longer range, while at the same time further developing the capability for nuclear retaliation

[981] The warning time for Norway and our allies has been reduced to hours and days

[982] In sum, Russian modernization has helped reduce NATO's conventional superiority, although the overall balance of power remains in Russia's disfavor

[983] Exercise Zapad in the fall of 2017 and exercise Ocean Shield in the Baltic Sea and the Norwegian Sea in late summer 2019 demonstrated the Russian armed forces' significantly increased combat power, ability to move quickly over large distances, and ability to deny allied forces access to the Norwegian Sea and the highlands

[984] Russian military forces thereby signaled that they could make American reinforcement of Europe challenging at short notice

[985] If Russia expands its bastion defense, a defense line could extend from the Norwegian Sea and westward via the United Kingdom and Iceland to Greenland, and Norway would be located behind Russia's advanced defense line

[986] This will have serious consequences for Norwegian freedom of action and security, and limit the alliance's opportunities to strengthen Norway

[987] The more strained relationship between Russia and Western countries means that this will once again become important in understanding Norway's security situation

[988] Bilateral military cooperation with Russia was suspended as a result of the illegal annexation of Crimea

[989] The direct line between the Norwegian Armed Forces' Operational Headquarters (FOH) and the Russian Northern Fleet, the cooperation related to the coast guard and border guard, the cooperation on search and rescue, and the mechanisms in the Incidents at Sea Agreement were nevertheless maintained in order to safeguard regional security and stability

[990] In addition, regular consultations are held at the ministerial level to exchange views and help increase understanding of our respective countries' policies

[991] In 2019, it was agreed to establish a communication channel between the defense leaderships in Oslo and Moscow in order to contribute to dialogue and prevent misunderstandings related to military activity

[992] Russia is facing a challenging period in terms of political and economic development and modernization of society and industry, but gives high priority to security and defense

[1204] Key areas for the sector's development

[1205] Technological development

[1206] The world is in a phase that many describe as the fourth industrial revolution

[1209] At the same time, major groundbreaking changes are also occurring in the form of the development of new technology, or completely new applications of known technology

[1210] Such breaches are more challenging to predict and handle

[1211] The pace of change is increasing within both of these development tracks

[1212] The increasing pace of change and spread of technology makes it difficult to predict in which technology areas the development will be greatest and have the greatest significance for the defense sector

[1213] Continued growth in the scale of data, computing power, and connectivity will continue to drive the development of artificial intelligence, autonomy, quantum computing, and automation

[1214] Increased use of this technology in information gathering and warfare could lead to concepts that are currently difficult to predict or imagine

[1215] At the same time, this development presents ethical, legal and political dilemmas that must be addressed

[1216] The changes are happening so quickly that there is a real danger that systems with great potential for harm will be put into use before international regulation of these is established

[1217] Global communication and information systems are leading to the spread of knowledge being faster than before and the difference between technology available for military and civilian purposes is being reduced in several areas

[1218] Large international technology companies are now leading in key areas of technology development

[1219] Continued growth is expected within communications technology, networks, data analysis and processing power

[1220] Together with developments in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation and synthetic biology, this could provide new opportunities and methods for the use of power

[1221] Even if commercial technology reaches a level of performance that makes it militarily relevant, the development does not necessarily lead to defense equipment becoming less expensive

[1222] Large, new weapons platforms are becoming increasingly advanced, contributing to rising costs

[1223] A challenge for small countries is that these platforms reach a price level that only allows them to be acquired in quantities below critical minimum values

[1224] Because development is happening faster than before, materials can also become outdated more quickly and thus have a reduced lifespan

[1225] Norwegian welfare and economic development depend on the opportunities that technology provides being utilized

[1226] Technological developments have significant implications for Norway as one of the world's most digitalized countries

[1227] As a result of society's pervasive digitalization, we are becoming more vulnerable

[1228] The use of network operations by state and non-state threat actors poses a significant risk to critical societal functions

[1229] As a result of the dependencies between the civilian and military sides, the overall consequences of our vulnerabilities must also be seen in a total defense context

[1230] Focusing on preventive security to reduce vulnerabilities across civilian and military sectors is therefore important

[1231] Digitalization is also hitting the defense sector with full force, and it is important to be able to digitalize while maintaining the security aspect

[1232] Sensors and effectors are connected in networks, enabling more efficient command and control

[1233] This will contribute to better situational understanding and increased ability for coordinated joint operational efforts

[1234] At the same time, the development of cost-effective commercially available technology provides new opportunities

[1235] For example, low-orbit satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles have reached a level of performance that was reserved for the great powers just a few years ago

[1236] Utilizing commercial technology strengthens the state's ability to monitor, early warn, and assert sovereignty in our strategic areas of interest

[1237] High technological change rates and diffusion provide new opportunities, but at the same time challenge the current regime for structural development, procurement and management of systems

[1238] The defense sector must be better positioned to implement technological generational shifts more quickly

[1239] At the same time, it is a resource challenge for Norway to follow developments across the entire range of military capabilities

[1240] This reinforces the need for multinational cooperation

[1241] The Armed Forces have significant potential in utilizing existing and new technology, and in combining technological advances in various areas

[1242] The defense sector must consider how it can be better structurally facilitated to ensure that appropriate and useful technologies are introduced and applied quickly

[1243] In this competition for technology, Norway has some comparative advantages that it is important to exploit, such as a great willingness and ability to adopt technological solutions, high technological competence in society, a tradition of cooperation between the military and civilian sides, and a high level of trust in society

[1244] Parallel development of concepts, doctrines, expertise and organization can provide increased effectiveness for defense capabilities

[1245] The Svendsen Committee has pointed out that the Armed Forces must improve its ability to recruit and retain personnel with relevant technological expertise, as there is increased competition in society for this type of expertise

[1246] This is one of several challenges posed by technological developments that the government will continue to work to find good solutions for in the future

[1247] Climate change and security

[1248] Climate change may become increasingly important for security and defense policy in the years ahead, and increasingly affect the ability of states to protect society and the population

[1249] Climate change can both have implications in terms of the causality of war and conflict, and pose a more direct challenge to military installations and operations

[1250] However, there is great uncertainty about how extensive the impact of climate change will be on security and defense policy, and in which areas the changes will have the greatest impact

[1251] This is related to the fact that it is difficult to predict exactly how big climate change will be in the coming decades, and it is uncertain to what extent states and societies will be able to handle the changes and their consequences without conflicts and security challenges arising

[1252] Climate change can be a threat multiplier

[1253] This means that climate change affects factors that can contribute to creating or intensifying conflicts, such as drought and desertification, melting ice and rising sea levels, floods and storms, as well as scarce access to natural resources such as water and land

[1254] Such deterioration of living conditions could trigger widespread migration, with the conflicts it could entail

[1255] For Norwegian security and defense policy, the effect of climate change in the High North is of particular importance

[1256] Melting of the ice could open up new activities and new players in an area of strategic importance for the major powers and of great importance to Norway

[1257] This may result in increased interest in potential natural resources, new sailing patterns and changes in the military presence in the region

[1258] The consequences of climate change in other areas of the world may also pose security challenges for Norway, as well as for allied countries

[1259] Wars and conflicts that have their root causes in whole or in part in climate change may create a need for and desire for assistance for more civilian and military crisis management in the years ahead

[1260] Climate change may also affect the Armed Forces' infrastructure, materiel and logistics

[1261] Among other things, challenges may arise related to handling higher sea levels, flooding, stormwater, strong winds, landslides and avalanches

[1262] In maintaining existing structures and in planning new buildings and facilities, one will have to take into account changed and more demanding weather and climate conditions

[1263] The defense sector will in future have a planned approach to climate and environmental measures

[1264] Through such measures, the sector will also contribute to the fulfillment of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[1265] The Corona pandemic and security

[1266] The coronavirus pandemic has exacerbated negative developments globally and regionally

[1267] It is too early to draw conclusions about what security policy consequences the corona pandemic may entail

[1268] It is nevertheless clear that the unpredictable dynamics that follow the pandemic have the potential to destabilize Norwegian and allied security

[1269] The great power rivalry has become even more evident

[1270] The deterioration of an already tense bilateral relationship between China and the United States has been pronounced

[1271] There has been very little cooperation between the major powers and few coordinated measures to slow the pandemic globally

[1272] The exchange of words between the United States, China and Russia has also intensified, and the crisis has provided greater scope for influence operations

[1273] The coronavirus pandemic has given threat actors the opportunity to exploit vulnerabilities and use complex tools with potentially destabilizing effects

[1274] This could have consequences for both Norwegian and allied security

[1275] A long-term health challenge such as the coronavirus pandemic will make it more demanding to maintain continuity in critical societal functions and defense capabilities over time

[1276] The pandemic has highlighted the importance of international cooperation, but at the same time revealed weaknesses in multilateral systems, especially during the initial phase of the pandemic

[1277] Several of the early crisis measures have led to restrictions on interaction with other countries

[1278] The World Health Organization has been criticized, and the EU's role was little visible in the early stages of the pandemic

[1279] European integration, transatlantic unity and international cooperation could be harmed

[1280] Over time, however, the EU has become much stronger and has helped to strengthen cooperation between European countries

[1281] State-supporting parties have strengthened in several countries since the crisis began

[1282] Increased nationalism and a lack of coordination of measures could have consequences for relations between states and regions

[1283] The economic consequences of the corona pandemic could reduce the political room for action for many countries and lead to social and political challenges for a long time to come

[1284] Closer international cooperation to prevent and mitigate global crises such as pandemics can have a positive effect in other areas

[1285] The balance between national emergency response solutions and strengthened international cooperation will be a key issue for most countries

[1286] The pandemic could also lead to greater coordination of measures and strategies to meet China's ambitions for increased global influence and rise

[1287] See Chapter 7, Text Box 7.5, for a detailed discussion of the consequences of the coronavirus pandemic for the Armed Forces and for the Armed Forces' assistance to other societal preparedness

[1288] Economic trends

[1289] There has been positive economic development in Norway over several years, but like our trading partners, we have recently been hit by a historically severe setback as a result of the corona pandemic and subsequent infection control measures

[1290] The economic recovery is underway, but activity levels will likely be lower than normal for several years to come

[1291] Norway has a small and open economy, and international developments therefore have a major impact on economic developments here at home

[1292] Furthermore, the security policy situation and changes therein could affect both international and national economic developments, and at the same time have an impact on national priorities

[1293] Changes in global and economic power relations can also create uncertainty in Norway

[1294] Trade policy conflicts have negatively affected international economic developments

[1295] The creation of new trade barriers and circumstances surrounding the UK's exit from the EU are examples of elements that increase uncertainty related to economic developments and that may weaken future prospects

[1296] In the slightly longer term, more challenges await

[1297] The same strong growth is not expected in the Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG) in the years ahead

[1298] The growth in the working-age population will be significantly weaker than before

[1299] In isolation, this will likely result in reduced room for manoeuvre in fiscal policy in the future

[1300] At the same time, there are significant constraints on budgets in the coming years, partly as a result of increased pension obligations

[1301] Furthermore, several of the government's long-term plans and goals, such as the National Transport Plan and other planned initiatives and ambitions, will require increased budgets in the coming years

[1302] If these are to be realized, the total costs could potentially be greater than the estimated room for maneuver resulting from revenue growth in the coming years

[1303] There will therefore be a need to increase revenues, reduce other expenses, implement the plans with fewer resources, or further improve public resource use

[1304] In the 2021 Perspective Report, the government will point out future challenges and how the government plans to meet them

[1305] Previous outlook reports have had a very long-term perspective, but this time the focus in the report is mainly on developments up to 2030, and the challenges Norway faces in the coming years

[1306] The economic issues must be considered in parallel with the security policy issues

[1307] Overall, this provides the basis for the priorities proposed for the defense sector in this proposal

[1308] Personnel and expertise

[1309] One of several key prerequisites for the defense sector to be able to meet higher operational requirements and tighter readiness times is sufficient access to personnel with relevant expertise

[1310] Today, there is a shortage of expertise in certain areas

[1311] This is partly due to the fact that certain areas of expertise are exposed to competition, but also because some departments are understaffed to begin with

[1312] Departments become vulnerable through absences related to, among other things, necessary education, certifications and leaves of absence

[1313] It is therefore necessary to both strengthen existing expertise and add new expertise

[1314] The labor market in Norway faces a number of challenges going forward

[1315] The population is aging, and pressure is increasing on the working population

[1316] There is an imbalance in the relationship between supply and demand in a number of areas of expertise

[1317] Several areas of society will need the same scarce resources

[1318] This also affects the defense sector

[1319] A challenge in recent years has been to retain the younger personnel serving in the operational departments

[1320] These personnel are in a phase of their careers that requires a lot of skill building

[1321] The Armed Forces produce their own expertise to a large extent

[1322] The result is high production pressure and high expenses, especially within vocational and functional education

[1323] These challenges are exacerbated for some personnel groups through high turnover and accelerated career progression

[1324] The sector has recently examined measures to contribute to an attractive and competitive specialist career in the Armed Forces

[1325] As part of this work, the reasons why personnel leave have been investigated

[1326] The picture is composite

[1327] Lack of career and development opportunities at lower levels is highlighted as an explanatory variable

[1328] The Armed Forces' career ladders are focused around management levels, while the professional career ladder currently appears unclear

[1329] Urbanization and centralization are also a strong and persistent trend that affects the labor market

[1330] Regional centers are growing while the number of jobs in rural areas is not keeping up

[1331] This trend reinforces the Armed Forces' challenges in retaining young personnel, and in creating a good balance between career and family life for other personnel

[1332] For example, it is more challenging to retain personnel in rural areas than at more urban-located bases, and the proportion of commuters to these bases is high

[1333] These are significant framework factors that, among other things, affect the ability to strengthen the presence in the North

[1334] The demographic trend with an increasing number of older workers will hit the defense sector with full force going forward

[1335] The consequence is that a large number of employees will retire in the coming years

[1336] This is both a challenge and an opportunity

[1337] On the one hand, this entails a comprehensive development of competence

[1338] On the other hand, it provides opportunities for structural adjustments that facilitate adapting the organization to new demands and expectations, especially related to technological developments

[1339] Ability to defend – willingness to be prepared – Further development of the defense economy Maintaining a defense that can handle changing challenges in the current threat landscape requires a continued willingness and ability to invest in the defense sector through adequate, stable and predictable financial frameworks

[1340] An important and necessary element of this is continued improvement and efficiency enhancement internally in the defense sector

[1341] To preserve economic sustainability in the development of the sector, there must be a balance between tasks of ambition, structure and economics

[1342] The previous long-term plan established a good foundation for sustainability in the defense economy in a long-term perspective, and the government thereby began necessary work to strengthen defense capabilities by improving availability, endurance and preparedness

[1343] It was decided to prioritize and catch up on maintenance backlogs, replenish spare parts and emergency stocks, increase activity, and invest in strategic capabilities that strengthen defense capabilities

[1344] In the period 2017–2020, the government has almost completed catching up on the backlog of maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks, and has at the same time built up a higher level of maintenance to avoid new backlogs building up

[1345] Standby times have been tightened and activity in the Armed Forces has increased significantly, while staffing has been increased for selected operational capacities

[1346] In addition, the government has initiated a large-scale renewal of the equipment

[1347] There has been a significant investment in the Armed Forces in the previous long-term plan, but the government has also been clear that this was the start of a more comprehensive and long-term effort to strengthen, modernize and further develop the defense sector

[1348] Implementation of the measures in the previous long-term plan also places financial constraints on the upcoming planning period

[1349] Initiated investments must be completed

[1350] The catch-up on maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks as well as the establishment and commissioning of new departments continues

[1351] The recommendations in this proposal are based on the fact that the measures already adopted and the decided arrangements will be continued

[1352] This is crucial for the further development of defense capabilities to better follow security policy developments

[1353] The drop in oil prices at the beginning of 2020 and the corona pandemic have also affected the defense economy

[1354] The large fluctuations in the Norwegian krone exchange rate, and the uncertainty surrounding the duration of the pandemic and any lasting consequences, are affecting defense planning

[1355] At the start of the second quarter, the Norwegian krone weakened sharply, especially against the US dollar and euro, while from the middle of the third quarter the Norwegian krone experienced a strengthening against the aforementioned currencies

[1356] An immediate consequence of the pandemic has been increased spending on infection control measures, while planned exercises have been canceled due to infection control concerns

[1357] The Armed Forces have also had reduced expenses as a result of reduced travel and lower activity

[1358] It is necessary for defense planning to take into account lasting shifts in economic framework conditions

[1359] At the same time, it will be very demanding to implement sound defense planning with a long-term perspective in light of changes in the economic outlook with unknown consequences and duration

[1360] Like the previous long-term plan, this one is also based on a carefully balanced and interdependent relationship between increased defense capacity, continuous improvement, and efficiency enhancement

[1361] Continuous improvement and efficiency enhancement are demanding, but also absolutely necessary to help cover increased expenses for prioritized purposes

[1362] Central to this long-term plan is that the work on modernization and reform should be ambitious, continuous and systematized

[1363] Through this, the work will overall contribute to reducing the need for increased defense frameworks, while at the same time supporting a sustainable defense structure

[1364] Norway is experiencing increased pressure from NATO and allies for further economic strengthening, also beyond the economic escalation path that was set as a basis

[1365] NATO's heads of state and government decided at the Wales Summit in 2014 to aim to move towards spending 2 percent of GDP on defense by 2024 (Defense Investment Pledge

[1366] This objective has been reiterated and reinforced during all subsequent summits

[1367] The defense sector's share of value creation in Norway Long-term planning until 2016 was largely based on the assumption of stability and low volatility in our local areas

[1368] In the decades following the end of the Cold War, the defense sector's share of both the state budget and GDP was significantly reduced

[1369] The government has reversed the previous trend of increasingly lower allocations to the defense sector relative to the state budget

[1370] Budget growth in the defense sector has been close to 30 percent since 2013, and defense spending's share of the state budget has increased from 3.6 percent to 4.3 percent during the same period

[1371] The deteriorating security situation in Europe, and the world at large, is being met with a significant investment in the Armed Forces and the sector as a whole

[1372] Details on financial conditions

[1373] Even after the significant budget growth in recent years, there is still a need to modernize and further develop the defense sector so that defense capabilities better respond to security policy developments

[1374] The previous long-term plan facilitated key decisions that set financial commitments for the period

[1375] These commitments constitute a starting point for this long-term plan

[1376] In addition, it will always be the case that reality may develop differently from what is planned and assumed

[1377] This means that at the beginning of the long-term planning period, several conditions and factors have been clarified that have influenced, and could influence, the defense economy and the economic scope for action in the future

[1378] The importance of the security situation for readiness requirements and for the defense economy The Armed Forces must be able to detect and handle incidents and events on a daily basis, and to act sufficiently quickly if a situation escalates and a crisis or armed conflict threatens

[1379] When the decision to build up forces is made, personnel who are not in daily service will be called up and equipped for missions in accordance with the Conscription Act

[1380] Equipment that is not in daily operation must be taken out of storage and prepared

[1381] This takes place during the department's on-call hours

[1382] Readiness time is therefore the time a given department has at its disposal from the time the decision to build up forces is made until the department is ready to carry out missions, cf. operational plans and imposed operational requirements in a crisis or war situation

[1383] However, a given standby time does not define requirements for the department's endurance, volume, or how any simultaneous situations should be handled

[1384] The latter factors will also be dimensional and have financial consequences, and will be particularly linked to the overall layout of the structure

[1385] Defense spending's share of the state budget and GDP

[1386] The shares for 2020 are based on the allocation level as of August of that year

[1387] Furthermore, defense spending has been corrected in line with the guidelines for measuring defense spending in NATO, see also box

[1388] It is important that the material is as close as possible to where the departments are set up, so that the withdrawal is as efficient as possible

[1389] Furthermore, supplies beyond what the departments have available for daily operations, such as sanitary equipment, food and ammunition, must be obtained either from the Armed Forces' emergency stockpiles or directly from manufacturers and suppliers

[1390] Strength building also means that the departments carry out the necessary exercises and training, so that they have a level of proficiency that satisfies the imposed operational requirements

[1391] Determination of readiness times is based on the prevailing situation and the operational plan

[1392] Secondly, the determination must take into account how resource-intensive it is to comply with the respective readiness times

[1393] Uptime is a product of several input factors; personnel, expertise, material availability and security of supply

[1394] Maintaining set up times therefore requires a balanced resource allocation between these input factors

[1395] It is possible to adjust the resource supply of the input factors, but some of these may have long lead times

[1396] For example, adding more personnel with the right expertise to the operational structure is a process that can take several years, as the necessary education, training and exercises are often time-consuming

[1397] Another challenge is that there is an interdependence between the various input factors

[1398] If material inventories are increased, there will be a need for expanded storage capacity and more personnel to operate the new material systems

[1399] Similarly, if the number of personnel is increased, the need for clothing and equipment, office space and barracks will increase, which in turn necessitates increased investment in, and operation of, property, buildings and facilities

[1400] The security policy situation is dynamic, and changes in it may mean that the objectives set for the long-term plan period are no longer as relevant or sufficient as when the plan was adopted

[1401] If the security situation worsens, it will require the Armed Forces' operational structure to have a higher operational tempo on a daily basis and shorter readiness times for operations in crisis and armed conflict

[1402] Higher daily operational tempo can lead to increased wear and tear on personnel and equipment, and thus the need for more available personnel, more equipment maintenance and increased spare parts inventories

[1403] Furthermore, there may be a risk that the departments are unable to carry out the necessary exercises and training to satisfy all operational requirements

[1404] The long-term plan's level of ambition and the determined use of resources to achieve given readiness times may prove to be insufficient if security policy developments take a further negative direction

[1405] In such a case, new assessments may be necessary related to possible reprioritization and any need for the provision of resources for on-call time-related purposes

[1406] However, the room for maneuver will be limited in the short term, partly due to the lead times for certain input factors

[1407] In the autumn of 2018, the NATO Secretary General urged allies to consider whether there are additional expenditures that should be included in the national reporting of defense spending to NATO, cf. the Defence Investment Pledge

[1408] The purpose of the review was to create confidence that the reporting reflects the actual expenditures spent on defense

[1409] Furthermore, the review should contribute to ensuring that allies report equally to the greatest extent possible

[1410] The review showed that some expenses budgeted in other ministries' budgets should be included and reported to NATO as defense expenses

[1411] According to NATO guidelines, expenses for the Rescue Helicopter Service, the Armed Forces Music's share under the Ministry of Culture, mandatory contributions to NATO's civilian budget and UN peacekeeping operations can be reported

[1412] It is planned to continue reporting expenses to the National Security Authority, even though responsibility has been transferred to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[1413] The review also revealed that Norway has reported too low a pension expenditure, which has therefore been adjusted

[1414] The changes in reporting to NATO meant that defense spending's share of GDP increased by about 0.2 percentage points

[1415] Furthermore, some changes are made to historical figures and projections, which make measuring the GDP share more accurate, and which is in line with how the majority of NATO countries do it

[1416] Due to this correction, there is a break in the above figure between

[1417] The figures for the years before 2013 cannot therefore be directly compared with the figures for 2013 and onwards

[1418] However, the work of revising reporting to NATO has not been completed

[1419] There are some additional expenditure categories that are under consideration and that may be included in reporting to NATO

[1420] Whether this will be done, however, depends on whether allies agree to change current practices regarding which expenses can be included

[1421] However, the work will only be completed after the NATO Secretary General has presented his final report

[1422] Currency exposure in the defense sector

[1423] Provisions for investments are a prerequisite for the production of defense capabilities

[1424] Investments in strategically important capabilities such as F-35 fighter jets and new maritime patrol aircraft are ongoing, and the focus on investing in strategic capabilities from the previous long-term plan will be continued and strengthened in the long-term plan period 2021–

[1425] Provisions for materiel investments will thus be increased, and based on the long-term plan period in 2021–2024, will average over 30 percent of the defense framework

[1426] A large proportion of material purchases are from suppliers outside Norway

[1427] This means that defense sector spending is significantly exposed to foreign currency

[1428] Historically, about 55 percent of material purchases have been exposed to foreign currency

[1429] For the defense sector, there is a risk associated with currency fluctuations

[1430] The government's approach to currency risk is in line with the self-insurer principle

[1431] As a result, businesses in the sector must themselves handle the unpredictability associated with currency fluctuations

[1432] Unpredictability is exacerbated by increased currency exposure, as a result of increased focus on procurement of new strategic capacities from foreign suppliers

[1433] There is a developing trend that new material systems are increasingly supported through operating agreements with suppliers

[1434] For the material systems delivered from abroad, the operating agreements will also be paid in foreign currency

[1435] The consequence is that some operating capital is increasingly exposed to foreign currency

[1436] In addition, Norwegian suppliers often use foreign suppliers in the production of goods and services

[1437] The defense sector's national procurement is therefore also indirectly affected by currency fluctuations

[1438] When determining the cost framework for a material project, a given exchange rate is used as the basis

[1439] Deviations from the assumed exchange rate, as a result of fluctuations in foreign currency, may lead to increased or reduced financing needs during the implementation of the acquisition

[1440] A weakened Norwegian krone can cause projects to become more expensive than planned

[1441] The consequences of this may be delays in implementation and/or changes in the scope/ambition of the project

[1442] This may also mean that other planned acquisitions or measures cannot be realized

[1443] In cases where the krone strengthens, a currency gain occurs

[1444] However, such a gain is difficult to take into account in an implementation perspective with long lead times

[1445] Constant need for improved material performance

[1446] Developments in the security policy situation and technological developments make it necessary to continuously modernize the structure and capabilities of the Armed Forces

[1447] The previous long-term plan was based on investments in, among other things, F-35 fighter jets, new submarines and new maritime patrol aircraft

[1448] Significant investments in ICT were also planned, among other things to achieve integration between the weapons platforms in the Armed Forces and with allies, in order to obtain maximum effect from these weapons systems

[1449] New, modern and upgraded weapons systems often have better performance than the equipment they replace, and such upgrades are necessary to further develop the Norwegian Armed Forces' operational capability, both nationally and in operations with our allies

[1450] There is a need to maintain the Armed Forces' operational capability and relative effectiveness compared to a potential adversary

[1451] Such maintenance of relative power creates a continuous need for upgrades, and constitutes a significant cost-driving factor

[1452] Military technology is often developed within relatively small markets and often has particularly high performance requirements

[1453] This also means that both the development and further development of military equipment are cost-intensive

[1454] This applies to both the shift between generations of main systems, such as combat aircraft and submarines, and upgrade needs within the life of the materiel system

[1455] Effective from 2017, the government has taken this cost growth element into account in defense planning

[1456] As a result of planned further development of the Armed Forces' structure and capacity, it is important for maintaining the Armed Forces' operational capability that such cost growth is also taken into account in the upcoming long-term planning period

[1457] Personnel expenses Personnel expenses constitute a significant proportion of the defense economy

[1458] The sector depends on a broad spectrum of expertise, and particularly within certain areas of expertise, market mechanisms put pressure on wages and working conditions

[1459] To recruit and retain critical expertise, the defense sector must be able to offer competitive frameworks

[1460] Continuous improvement and efficiency enhancement

[1461] Over time, the defense sector has worked systematically to free up resources for higher priority activities

[1462] The resources released from the improvement and efficiency work are retained in the sector and are thus sufficient to both cover the continuation of the government's debureaucratization and efficiency reform and help finance new initiatives within the defense sector

[1463] In the upcoming long-term plan period, the defense sector will be further developed through increased professionalization and modernization

[1464] Going forward, the government will emphasize improvements in the sector's deliveries by streamlining value chains and improving collaboration in the defense sector

[1465] The pace of change is driven particularly by technological developments

[1466] Important prerequisites for success include the sector's ability and potential to utilize both existing and new technology, increased professionalization, further developing the use of civilian actors, and proper organization, process development, and division of labor in the sector

[1467] The Ministry of Defense has, with professional support from FFI, and in dialogue with affected agencies, identified new areas of action within improvement and efficiency for the period 2021–

[1468] The work is presented in FFI report 19/01934, "How to create economic room for maneuver in the new long-term plan

[1469] Potential for improvement and efficiency 2021–

[1470] The report points to a range in the potential for lasting resource release from 1.6 to 3 billion 2020 kroner by the end of 2024, and presents improvements in the quality of the sector's deliveries within several of the sector's key business areas

[1471] Improvements in operational procurement, more efficient utilization of the sector's property, buildings and facilities, better implementation of material procurement and facilitation of operations, and generally better utilization of digital tools have been identified as areas with potential for improvement and efficiency enhancement

[1472] In this long-term plan, the government assumes that through work on continued improvement and efficiency in the sector, at least 1.9 billion 2020 kroner will be released by the end of 2024, which will contribute to priority areas in the sector

[1473] The scope of planned profit withdrawals increases annually from an initial level in 2021 of around Norwegian kroner 200 million

[1474] Several of the identified measures will require restructuring funds to be implemented

[1475] This means that the implementation of such measures will be included in the prioritization of investment measures in the defense sector

[1476] Planned resource release is increasing throughout the period, as shown

[1477] Estimated restructuring costs have been set aside early in the period to facilitate the implementation of the improvement and efficiency work

[1478] Box 4.2 Currency challenge in the current long-term plan

[1479] About 26 percent of the defense budget for 2020 is related to investments in new equipment

[1480] For material procurement excluding the fighter aircraft procurement, total currency exposure is estimated at approximately 55 percent, while approximately 90 percent of the costs of the fighter aircraft procurement are directly exposed to currency

[1481] The material is acquired in different currencies, with a particular scope in US dollars, euros, Swedish kroner and British pounds

[1482] Given the financial framework in the long-term plan for future material investments, and currency exposure as stated above, a deviation of 5 percent in exchange rates will result in an annual increased or reduced financing requirement of approximately NOK 800 million

[1483] The fall in oil prices at the beginning of 2020 and the corona pandemic have led to large fluctuations in the Norwegian krone exchange rate

[1484] The Norwegian krone weakened sharply against the US dollar and euro, among other things, and the weakening was over 15 percent by the end of April compared to the budget exchange rates used as the basis for the balanced budget

[1485] Given the financial framework in the long-term plan for future material investments, and currency exposure as stated above, a sustained weakening of the Norwegian krone corresponding to this level will result in annual additional expenses of approximately NOK 2.7 billion

[1486] At the same time, the Norwegian krone has, as of August 2020, strengthened against both the US dollar and the euro

[1487] The Norwegian krone has strengthened against the US dollar to a level that corresponds to the budget exchange rate that was used as the basis for the balanced budget for 2020, while the Norwegian krone against the euro, as of August 2020, was still weaker than the level assumed in the balanced budget

[1488] These fluctuations underscore the unpredictability that exists in the defense sector related to currency exposure

[1489] This is addressed in the annual budget process

[1524] A further economic boost for the defense sector

[1525] The government's central goal for the defense sector is that missions can be solved within a comprehensive and responsible framework, in the short and long term

[1526] Long-termism and predictability of the economic framework conditions are necessary premises for the implementation of the long-term plan, and the perspective in the long-term plan necessarily extends beyond the first four-year period

[1527] In the proposal, the government assumes a continued focus on the defense sector through a further strengthening of the defense budget, together with a number of resource-freeing measures

[1528] The extensive cost calculations that form the basis for the decisions put forward in this proposal are based on a number of assumptions and foundation work, including the expected status of the previous long-term plan at the end of the year

[1529] However, the implementation of the previous long-term plan for the period 2017–2020 has made it clear that several of the underlying assumptions have changed or have not materialized as expected, and has thus created a different economic starting point, to which this long-term plan relates

[1530] In addition, the Norwegian krone has weakened over time against relevant foreign currencies

[1531] Within the significant increase in the defense budget that the government is now proposing, it has therefore been necessary to find room for financing operations, which in some areas have become more expensive than previously anticipated

[1532] In sum, a good starting point is established for further strengthening of the defense sector with increased operational capability in the Armed Forces, and a long-term balance between tasks with ambitions, structure and finances

[1533] The long-term plan envisages the smoothest possible financial escalation of the increase in appropriations for defence purposes, but it is taken into account that larger investment expenditures may fall in certain budget years

[1534] The Government will therefore return to the specific escalation in each budget

[1535] The aim is for the defense budget in 2028 to be 16.5 billion kroner 2020 above the adopted budget

[1536] This involves a significant strengthening of the defense budget in the period 2021–2024, with a budget level in 2024 that is approximately 8.3 billion kroner above the adopted budget

[1557] Maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks In the previous long-term plan, it was confirmed that the Armed Forces' emergency preparedness and requirements for readiness times had not been given the necessary priority until then

[1558] A backlog related to maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks was pointed out

[1559] Since 2017, the government has prioritized increased availability and endurance for the Armed Forces' capabilities, and a lot of resources have been used to make the defense we have work

[1560] This includes catching up on maintenance backlogs, while spare parts stocks and emergency stocks have been built up

[1561] Catching up on the backlog is essential as a contribution to the lasting strengthening of operational capability

[1562] The work has already had a good effect

[1563] During the same period, the government has financed a permanently higher level of maintenance, compared to before 2017, to avoid new backlogs building up

[1564] However, some of the main challenges for operational capability are still related to preparedness for crisis and armed conflict, as maintaining and strengthening the Armed Forces' ability for national preparedness for security policy crises and armed conflict is resource-demanding

[1565] It is therefore crucial that the focus on maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks continues

[1566] Increased staffing and activity

[1567] In the previous long-term plan, emphasis was placed on strengthening staffing in the operational part of the structure, through the transfer of resources from management and base operations to operational activities

[1568] An increased focus on training and education of personnel was also assumed

[1569] The government plans to increase staffing in the Armed Forces from

[1570] Increased personnel volume will gradually provide stronger operational capability, and contribute to increased national preparedness, responsiveness and endurance

[1571] The government will also continue its focus on exercises and training

[1572] The heightened security situation makes it necessary to plan for tighter readiness times, which requires higher personnel availability

[1573] For some departments, practice and training will be further strengthened to reach a satisfactory level of training

[1574] Investments in new equipment

[1575] The previous long-term plan laid the foundation for the start of investments in strategic capabilities, including investments in F-35 fighter jets and new maritime patrol aircraft

[1576] For the long-term plan period 2021–2024, it is planned that payments for material investments will increase further

[1577] Maritime patrol aircraft, new submarines, supply readiness and increased material supplies to Brigade North are the most resource-intensive areas

[1578] Based on this long-term plan, and as a share of the total defense budget, investments will average over 30 percent in the years up to and including

[1579] However, it is not until 2023 that investments increase significantly compared to the assumptions from the previous long-term plan

[1580] Already planned and new investment projects will result in increased operating expenses

[1581] In the first years of the new long-term plan, significant funds have been set aside to achieve the planned effect from the material investment projects

[1582] This includes, among other things, more maintenance, more spare parts and expenses related to practice and training

[1583] In the previous long-term plan, cost growth was taken into account as a consequence of maintaining the relative effectiveness of the Armed Forces' platforms

[1584] It was acknowledged that the defense sector is facing a unique cost increase related to the phasing in of high-tech and highly advanced equipment

[1585] This applies to both the shift between generations of main systems, such as combat aircraft and submarines, and upgrade needs within the life of the materiel system

[1586] This long-term plan also takes into account such cost growth

[1587] Further development of infrastructure

[1588] The defense sector holds a significant and varied property portfolio with a variety of different properties, buildings and facilities, from military facilities and runways to homes and office buildings

[1589] In total, this amounts to about 4 million square meters of property

[1590] Expenditure on investments and operation of the sector's property portfolio constitutes around 15 percent of the defense budget, and measures to improve resource use within the sector's property, buildings and structures will also be important in this long-term planning period

[1591] A report from the Norwegian Defence Research Institute from 2018 (FFI report 18/00498) points out that the property has a significant maintenance backlog and needs upgrading

[1592] This indicates that too few resources have been spent on maintenance over time

[1593] During this long-term plan period, it will be possible to provide infrastructure in new ways, and demanding priorities will be made for both investment and operating funds for property, buildings and facilities to help improve the condition of the sector's infrastructure

[1594] Higher priority investment needs directly linked to operational capacities

[1595] However, it will make it challenging in the short term to significantly improve the condition of existing buildings and facilities, while in the somewhat longer term, measures will be taken to improve the situation

[1596] Part II Development of the overall defence capability Competence – a fundamental prerequisite for strengthening the Armed Forces

[1597] Personnel are the Armed Forces' most important resource

[1598] When the Armed Forces' operational capability is to be strengthened, it is crucial that personnel with the right expertise and the right composition man the sector's organization, materiel and systems

[1599] The needs of the Armed Forces must guide the sizing of the personnel and expertise structure

[1600] At the same time, the structure must be adjusted and balanced so that it can meet both current and future needs in the most flexible way possible

[1601] The government has implemented a number of comprehensive reforms in the area of personnel and expertise, including the military system (cf. Bill No

[1602] LS (2014–2015), the education reform and the further development of general conscription and initial service (cf. Prop

[1603] S (2015–2016) and Prop

[1604] S (2017–

[1605] Several strategic initiatives and measures have also been implemented, such as the reduction of staff and support functions and the reorganization of HR services

[1606] The defense sector has put in significant work in implementing these reforms, and the necessary further development of this area in the defense sector will take place with these reforms and measures as a platform

[1607] Strengthened staffing The Government plans to increase staffing in selected areas from 2021 to strengthen the response capacity and endurance of the Armed Forces

[1608] The increased staffing will primarily involve more specialists and conscripts in their first year of service

[1609] The majority of the new positions are prioritized for operational units

[1610] In the Army, the increased staffing will mainly be in Brigade Nord and Finnmark Land Defence

[1611] For the Air Force, the increased manning is prioritized primarily for air defense, base defense and support of the F

[1612] The Navy is planning, among other things, to strengthen the vessel crews

[1613] To strengthen responsiveness and endurance, it is also necessary to strengthen leadership and support capabilities

[1614] It is therefore planned to strengthen the Armed Forces' operational headquarters, to strengthen the Cyber Defence with more employees for the Cyber Security Centre and to increase staffing at the National Logistics Centre in the Armed Forces' Logistics Organisation

[1615] The planned staffing increase must be seen in the context of new investments and capacities being phased in, as well as the further development of the Armed Forces' education system

[1616] To support sustainable development of the defense sector, it is important that the increase in staffing is balanced against other input factors and the organization's ability to develop expertise

[1617] The educational capacity is being strengthened to support the staffing of the Armed Forces

[1618] This will take time, and capacity will be increased gradually from

[1619] The number of cadets and students at the Norwegian Armed Forces College, including the military academies and the staff school, will be increased somewhat, but the Armed Forces primarily need more specialists and conscripts in their first year of service

[1620] Recruit training is provided by operational departments

[1621] Capacity is being strengthened through the establishment of a new joint recruit school at Terningmoen, in addition to the recruit school at Madla

[1622] This is also an important step to increase the availability and responsiveness of the standing operational departments in the Armed Forces

[1623] The capacity of the Armed Forces' officer training is being strengthened to train more officers

[1624] The level-building education for commanders and other specialists is being strengthened to provide necessary professional education within the framework of the scheme for military employees

[1625] Subject- and functional-oriented education is being strengthened throughout the Armed Forces

[1626] In the implementation of the long-term plan, the Chief of Defence will further detail the staffing increases, including adjusting the educational capacity and educational volume within the priorities that the government has set in the long-term plan
