[1629] Facilitate the necessary expertise

[1630] The main message from the Svendsen Committee is that the Armed Forces deliver operational capability every day, but that technological developments challenge the organization of the Armed Forces' activities, the cultural understanding of what is important, and how and what competence must be developed and managed

[1631] It is emphasized that the Armed Forces cannot meet the need for increased staffing by simply doing more of the same

[1632] Traditional structures that can hinder competence development and diversity must be broken down

[1633] The committee believes that the Armed Forces have made choices that result in the organization not being provided with relevant expertise and diversity that is necessary to develop the business based on changing requirements, needs and a constantly changing threat landscape, and has proposed a number of specific measures

[1634] After the hearing, the Ministry of Defence will decide how the report will be included in the further work to further develop the personnel and competence area in the sector

[1635] To facilitate a relevant personnel and expertise structure in the defense sector, the Armed Forces need increased access to society's overall expertise pool

[1636] Closer cooperation and more expertise flow between the defense sector and civilian sectors will help meet the sector's expertise needs, as well as give civilian sectors better access to expertise from the Armed Forces

[1637] This will provide a broader anchoring of the Armed Forces throughout society and be important for the further development of total defense cooperation

[1638] The Government will further develop the personnel and competence area to ensure that the defense sector has the necessary flexibility to quickly adapt to new competence needs under changing conditions and framework conditions

[1639] The defense sector should be a modern and attractive employer, offering each employee flexibility and development opportunities

[1640] The defense sector must work to have high legitimacy, a good reputation and trust among the population

[1641] Three main approaches are central to achieving these goals

[1642] Firstly, more flexible staffing concepts must be developed

[1643] Increased staffing cannot be solved with more permanent employees alone

[1644] It is necessary to supplement with several ways of staffing to achieve the desired effect, without taking too much risk

[1645] Secondly, the ability to recruit and retain personnel must be strengthened

[1646] Thirdly, arrangements must be made for the efficient and flexible development and utilization of expertise

[1647] Development and application of flexible staffing concepts

[1648] The Armed Forces' manning concepts must be a result of the operational requirements placed on the force structure

[1649] Further development and increased utilization of conscription, the reservist system, and cooperation arrangements with allies, the business community, civilian educational institutions, and other sectors are necessary areas of focus to increase access to relevant expertise

[1650] The staffing concepts for each department must also be reviewed against requirements for responsiveness

[1651] Departments with high requirements for responsiveness will need a different composition of personnel categories than departments with lower requirements for responsiveness

[1652] Strengthen the relevance of conscription for staffing permanent departments

[1653] Conscription gives the Armed Forces access to personnel and expertise to staff the Armed Forces' force structure

[1654] Conscription lays the foundation for the force structure to be increased in both breadth and depth when needs change

[1655] Thus, conscription can be seen as a national emergency system that contributes to the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks

[1656] The first-aid service must be organized in a way that maintains the necessary operational capability throughout the year

[1657] With current practice, large parts of the conscripts who are due for initial service are replaced at the same time

[1658] In addition, the operational departments provide basic education

[1659] This was also the reason why the government introduced a new system for conscription and initial service in the Army, see the Storting's consideration of Recommendation

[1660] S (2017–2018) to Prop

[1661] S (2017–

[1662] To strengthen the flexibility and relevance of conscription for staffing permanent departments, the government recommends further developing conscription and initial service for the entire Armed Forces in line with the principles already adopted for the Army

[1663] In order to maintain sufficient and stable operational capability, conscripts for initial service shall be distributed over two or more indents per year

[1664] The number of rotations and timing of indentation must be adapted to the needs of the respective departments

[1665] Basic training should, as a general rule, be conducted outside the operational departments

[1666] The length of the initial service shall, as a general rule, be 12 and 16 months

[1667] months of initial service will be most relevant in departments with high requirements for competence and joint training

[1668] Increased use of reservists and introduction of an active reserve throughout the Armed Forces

[1669] Through the previous long-term plan, the government has set an increased ambition for the use of reservists and a revitalization of the reservist concept

[1670] Reservists are a key element in building robustness and endurance in the structure of the Armed Forces

[1671] Reservists can be used during force buildup and in extraordinary events, but can also be used more flexibly to meet multiple competence needs, nationally and internationally

[1672] As part of this work, an active reserve has been introduced for the Army. Recommendation

[1673] S (2017–2018) to Prop

[1674] The government is introducing an active reserve throughout the Armed Forces

[1675] The active reserve helps ensure that the departments have the necessary volume and expertise to maintain national preparedness

[1676] The active reserve shall be trained and practiced as an integrated part of the departments, and called into service when necessary

[1677] There may also be some servicemen on contract in the active reserve, for example within special areas of expertise where the Armed Forces do not develop expertise themselves

[1678] An important part of the active reserve is the effort reserve

[1679] The operational reserve is an essential element in strengthening the Armed Forces' ability to respond quickly and simultaneously across the entire spectrum of crises, both nationally and internationally

[1680] The operational reserve will therefore primarily consist of personnel who have entered into a contract for service as a reservist in the Armed Forces

[1681] Need for more reservists on contract The use of reservists on contract is an important measure for the Armed Forces to be able to draw on larger parts of society's expertise and to be able to scale capacity within certain areas of expertise

[1682] The Armed Forces have a complex portfolio of tasks, and the breadth of the need for expertise can in many ways be compared to the diversity in demand in society at large

[1683] In addition, the Armed Forces need expertise that is largely of a civilian nature

[1684] In addition to knowing their civilian profession, personnel must also master basic military skills to be able to operate in crisis and armed conflict

[1685] The supply of personnel who master both of these dimensions is currently limited and must therefore be strengthened

[1686] The Armed Forces depend on recruiting personnel with both military and civilian qualifications, not only for permanent positions, but also as reservists

[1687] Military service is the main basis for recruitment

[1688] At the same time, military service has some overall frameworks for lengths of service and age that make it necessary to use contracts in addition

[1689] A contract-based service obligation provides greater flexibility than the service obligation that results from conscription, both in terms of requirements for notice periods, training patterns, assignment portfolio and age

[1690] A contract for compulsory service as a reservist in the Armed Forces entails significant obligations for the individual and consequences for third parties, such as the main employer and family

[1691] Allowing the use of contract-based reservists throughout the Armed Forces, to carry out missions based on the Armed Forces' needs, is being considered for regulation in a separate legal basis in the Defence Act

[1692] A proposal for such a legal basis has been subject to broad public consultation, and the Ministry of Defence is now considering the consultation inputs before a bill is finalized

[1693] The government will strengthen incentives for personnel in the reserve

[1694] First and foremost, so that the obligation imposed by society does not become an unreasonable burden on the individual, but also because a well-functioning reservist concept requires motivated service members who willingly report for duty when the need arises

[1695] Today's compensation model is fragmented, resource-intensive and results in large differences between the compensation of privates on the one hand, and officers and commanders on the other

[1696] Common to both privates, officers and commanders is that the compensation is independent of civilian income

[1697] The government recommends introducing a new remuneration model for reservists based on income compensation

[1698] This means, among other things, that those subject to compulsory service can have lost income as a result of performing their service covered by up to six times the basic amount of the National Insurance scheme

[1699] The introduction of a new remuneration model involves harmonization with the remuneration model that was introduced for the Civil Defence in 2018, cf. regulations on remuneration for service in the Civil Defence

[1700] This means that personnel on duty are remunerated according to the same principles regardless of which emergency services agency they represent

[1701] Strengthened cooperation with civilian employers

[1702] A central part of a comprehensive reservist concept is solid support and collaboration with the employer, including to create understanding of the social mission that reservists fulfill

[1703] The defense sector and the private sector are dependent on being able to benefit from each other's expertise

[1704] Several NATO countries have established their own Employer Support organizations to better link the military and civilian sides in the personnel area

[1705] In several countries, this type of organization also has a dedicated responsibility towards the business community to highlight the expertise of reservists and veterans

[1706] The Government will facilitate a targeted effort for better civil-military cooperation within the personnel area

[1707] This should be exercised based on principles of good governance, including that caution is exercised when employees change jobs between customer and supplier to prevent insider trading and impartiality problems

[1708] Strengthening the ability to recruit and retain personnel To strengthen the ability to recruit and retain personnel, the defense sector must offer attractive and competitive career opportunities for both military and civilian personnel

[1709] The defense sector should be a safe and inclusive workplace where there is zero tolerance for bullying and harassment

[1710] More targeted recruitment The Armed Forces currently select motivated candidates with good grades and a high level of ability for initial service

[1711] Approximately three out of five people who are accepted into the first-time service have a specialization in studies from upper secondary school

[1712] This personnel currently forms the main basis for further recruitment into the specialist corps

[1713] There is good recruitment for several of the specialist positions

[1714] However, experience shows that when the Armed Forces recruit personnel with academic and leadership ambitions for specialist positions at the operational level, these individuals are often lost after a short time

[1715] More differentiated recruitment, for example increased attention to the recruitment of people with a vocational education background for initial service, could counteract this

[1716] The work that has been initiated to further develop recruitment processes must continue so that the defense sector demands the right expertise

[1717] This applies in particular to selection for the specialist corps and civilian employment, where the Armed Forces must consider the possibility of recruiting a greater diversity of the population through a critical review of position requirements

[1718] Today, much of the recruitment for the specialist corps takes place locally in the department and is aimed at conscripts who are in for their first service

[1719] This must be strengthened, also when it comes to recruitment based on geographical affiliation

[1720] In addition, all the opportunities in the Armed Forces must be made visible to a wider audience through increased use of digital services

[1721] Competence, equality and diversity In order to be able to solve tasks and fulfill social responsibility in the best possible way, the defense sector needs personnel with varied backgrounds and competence

[1722] The sector must therefore utilize a broad recruitment base to facilitate the necessary diversity of expertise

[1723] It is important that employees in the defense sector reflect the diversity elsewhere in society

[1724] Diversity in the sector must accommodate a broad spectrum of cultures, identities and expertise

[1725] The defense sector will continue its work on gender equality, with particular emphasis on increasing the proportion of women in the organization. Therefore, the government has set a goal of at least 30 percent of both genders in officer and war academy education

[1726] The work supports the UN's Sustainable Development Goals on gender equality

[1727] Increased diversity requires expertise in culture and diversity and change management

[1728] This will be followed up through strategic work on attitudes, ethics and leadership in the sector

[1729] Efforts to prevent and deal with bullying and harassment are an important part of this work

[1730] Sexual harassment is an obstacle to safe and real participation in all areas of society, including the Armed Forces

[1731] The work of preventing and dealing with sexual harassment should continue to have a high priority

[1732] Work is underway to further develop clear guidelines and reduce the threshold for reporting objectionable matters

[1733] Military service provides a good basis for attracting other types of competences than those that are primarily selected today

[1734] An example is the need for digital competence

[1735] Necessary growth within this area of the defense sector puts pressure on one of the areas of expertise where civilian society also experiences a shortage of resources

[1736] The Armed Forces should therefore exploit the opportunities offered by conscription to attract, among other things, digital expertise

[1737] This requires that the Armed Forces must rethink competence requirements in connection with selection for initial service

[1738] A targeted effort to attract people with different characteristics will be part of the effort to close the skills gap

[1739] Initial service is one of several possible paths to both the officer and specialist corps

[1740] Strengthening within the personnel area cannot be solved through traditional recruitment and education alone and requires new and more offensive thinking about recruitment and re-recruitment

[1741] The potential for recruiting people with relevant civilian expertise and experience is great

[1742] Several of these will have completed initial service and can be employed directly as military personnel, while other groups can be offered the necessary basic military training as needed

[1743] A clear focus on tapping the recruitment potential in these groups could help meet the Armed Forces' skills needs

[1744] It is also a measure to balance a large educational need within the Armed Forces and create the most balanced age structure possible

[1745] A prerequisite for such recruitment is that the civilian competence that the individual brings with them is recognized and provides value for further professional careers

[1746] Change to the Armed Forces' special age limit

[1747] The pension reform facilitates a pension system that it is possible to pay for in the future

[1748] An important element is to get people to stay in work longer, both through financial incentives and through higher retirement ages

[1749] For the defense sector, this is an opportunity because it facilitates the retention of important expertise in a longer perspective, and a challenge because the Armed Forces depend on a relatively young personnel pool to meet operational requirements

[1750] In the defense sector, military personnel are the largest occupational group with a special age limit

[1751] The age limit for military personnel has been changed a number of times

[1752] However, the rationale for the age limit has remained largely unchanged

[1753] The need for a balanced age and rank structure as a premise for operational capability and readiness has been a consistent argument

[1754] This also includes the organizational perspective and the employer's management ability to adapt the organization of the personnel structure

[1755] For operational and emergency preparedness reasons, the Norwegian Armed Forces have a functional need for an employer-controlled retirement mechanism, with an obligation to retire for all or parts of the occupational group in the upper age categories

[1756] At the same time, there is room for alternative solutions to the current model

[1757] The Government therefore assumes that the Armed Forces' special age limit will be changed during this long-term plan period

[1758] The Government will return to the Storting with a proposal for legislative change

[1759] Incentives to retain personnel

[1760] The defense sector invests heavily in education and training activities for its employees

[1761] Lack of education leads to absence from the departments

[1762] This reduces opportunities for training and building competence in the departments, and it increases work pressure on those who remain

[1763] Reduced termination rates and increased service time will thus have great value both for the use of resources for education and training, and for the pool of expertise

[1764] Career and skills development opportunities are important motivational factors for staying in a workplace

[1765] Given the changes resulting from the military system, efforts to highlight the opportunities across the sector are crucial

[1766] This applies particularly to career opportunities as a specialist

[1767] The salary and incentive systems should be further developed in line with new needs

[1768] For example, there may be a need for greater differentiation, including a more targeted use of instruments towards critical expertise, areas of expertise exposed to competition, and services in rural areas

[1769] The Ministry of Defence has initiated work to establish a better knowledge base for further work on pay and incentives

[1770] Facilitate the efficient and flexible development and utilization of expertise. In order to fulfill its social responsibility, the defense sector must perform its tasks and manage its resources in a way that creates trust, support and legitimacy in the population

[1771] This requires continuous attention to values and organizational culture

[1772] Leaders and employees in the defense sector must be able to perform their tasks in a way that reflects society's norms, values ​​and expectations

[1773] Based on this basic foundation, systems for developing competence, and the competence of individual employees, must be further developed to meet the needs of the sector

[1774] Competence from a technology perspective

[1775] Technology can help strengthen the Armed Forces' operational capacity in a cost-effective manner

[1776] For example, autonomous systems can contribute to presence and data collection on a scale that would be prohibitive for manned systems and thereby contribute to increased situational awareness

[1913] Utilization of technology

[1914] There is significant potential in better utilization of both existing and new technology

[2023] Society's resilience and total defense

[2024] A complex threat landscape requires coordinated security and preparedness

[2025] A modern and prepared total defense strengthens the nation's resilience and endurance, and reduces vulnerability to complex threats

[2026] The Total Defense Concept supports both our national defense capability, our collective capability in NATO, and our reinforcement agreements and relationships with close allies

[2027] The concept of civil-military cooperation in principle encompasses all cooperation at all levels and spans a broad field with many different actors

[2028] The content of the Total is largely situational

[2029] The Total Defence Concept is part of civil-military cooperation, but is limited to encompassing mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society related to incidents and crises throughout the entire crisis spectrum from peace to security policy crisis and armed conflict

[2030] Total defense shall ensure the best possible utilization of society's limited resources in terms of prevention, emergency planning, crisis management and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum

[2031] Total defence can thus serve as a superstructure and a tool for a number of activities such as work on preventive security, complex threats and comprehensive situational awareness, which this chapter will discuss in more detail

[2032] Civil-military cooperation also includes other cooperation between civilian and military actors that is not directly related to crises and armed conflict

[2033] An example is the Coast Guard's supervisory authority within fishing and trapping, environmental protection and customs

[2034] Civil-military cooperation is becoming increasingly important for the defense of Norway

[2035] Increasing geopolitical tension, combined with greater complexity in the threat landscape and dependencies across sectors of society, makes close cooperation between civilian and military authorities increasingly important

[2036] This requires shared recognition of the challenges associated with the cross-sectoral threat landscape

[2037] There has been significant development and progress in civil-military cooperation within the framework of the total defense concept in recent years

[2038] Experience from this work and developments in the threat landscape nevertheless indicate that there is a need for further development and improvements within the total defence arrangements

[2039] A more unclear and unpredictable threat landscape reduces the distinction between societal security and state security and increases the interdependence between the two security concepts

[2040] Available resources with high responsiveness require good resource utilization and coordination across sectors and levels

[2041] Increased involvement of civilian actors in the operational activities of the Norwegian Armed Forces and allies, as demonstrated during the NATO exercise Trident Juncture 2018, underlines this need

[2042] Civil-military cooperation must be developed holistically and continuously so that vulnerabilities across state and societal security are reduced

[2043] A broader spectrum of vulnerabilities and opportunities for hostile use of instruments, from both state and non-state actors, can affect across sectors

[2044] Individual incidents can occur in different sectors, within private and public sectors, and at different times

[2045] This can make it more challenging to uncover whether a single incident is part of a more complex use of instruments, and also makes it more challenging to establish a comprehensive understanding of the situation

[2046] The combined use of instruments helps to blur the distinctions between peace and conflict

[2047] Exploitation of vulnerabilities can occur even in peacetime with major consequences for the Armed Forces' operational capability

[2048] Composite, cross-sectoral threats are nothing new, but they have become a more prominent feature of today's security policy landscape

[2049] Rapid technological development and shorter warning times make the threat landscape more complex and increase the importance of preventive security work

[2050] Preventive security

[2051] The Government will strengthen the defense sector's ability to protect its assets

[2052] A prerequisite for maintaining civilian support for national and allied military forces throughout the entire crisis spectrum is that civilian sectors secure their assets worthy of protection in a responsible manner

[2053] Total defense depends on civilian and military actors reducing their vulnerabilities and having a reasonable level of basic security

[2054] The purpose of preventive security work is to protect national security interests against intentional actions that could directly or indirectly harm them

[2055] This means that there is a clear connection between the Armed Forces' tasks and capabilities, and preventive security work

[2056] The National Security Act (the National Security Act) is one of the most important administrative and legal instruments the state has within preventive security

[2057] National security, as the term is used in the Security Act, is the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[2058] The national security interests are defined as the country's sovereignty, territorial integrity and democratic form of government and overall security policy interests related to: a) the activities, security and freedom of action of the highest state bodies, b) defense, security and preparedness, c) relations with other states and international organizations, d) economic stability and freedom of action and e) the basic functionality of society and the basic security of the population

[2059] The scope of the Security Act is the area of state security and that part of the area of societal security that is of significant importance to the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[2060] The Security Act requires the identification of fundamental national functions

[2061] These are functions that, if completely or partially eliminated, will weaken the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[2062] All ministries are in the process of identifying the basic national functions in their sectors

[2063] Through leveling and mapping of connections and dependencies between these, an overview will be established of which functions support national security interests on the civilian and military side

[2064] The Armed Forces identify their dependence on critical infrastructure in other sectors, so that the responsible sector ministry can assess whether the relevant infrastructure should be subject to the Security Act if it is not already so

[2065] In the defense sector, five basic national functions with associated sub-functions have been identified

[2066] These are directly related to the tasks of the Armed Forces

[2067] If the tasks and capabilities of the Armed Forces change, the sector's basic national functions will change accordingly

[2068] Comprehensive safety management is a fundamental prerequisite for success in preventive safety work

[2069] This involves looking at physical, digital, human and organizational measures in context

[2070] Agencies in the defense sector must view preventive security work in the context of other business management and the assessment of operational capability

[2071] This requires, among other things, that agencies in the defense sector have leaders with a conscious approach to risk management

[2072] It is also necessary to have personnel who have good expertise in the security field, and who are placed correctly in the structure so that they can support the management level in a good way

[2073] The Armed Forces depend on information and information systems to be able to carry out their tasks and to be able to conduct operations effectively

[2074] At the same time, information systems and infrastructures are vulnerable to unwanted digital incidents

[2075] To help maintain the Armed Forces' freedom of action in the digital space, the basic security in the defence sector's information systems must ensure a reasonable level of security and that the risk is acceptable

[2076] The renewal of the defense sector's communication and information systems will help to phase out or replace systems that do not meet security requirements

[2077] When planning and developing new information systems, it must be assessed whether the system is worthy of protection, and the systems must be secured accordingly

[2078] Unwanted digital incidents must be detected and handled

[2079] Basic national functions in the defense sector

[2080] The ability for intelligence, situational awareness and timely warning GNF

[2081] The ability to handle incidents and security policy crises and, if necessary, defend Norwegian or allied territory

[2082] Command and control The ability to command and control Norwegian and allied forces

[2083] The ability to protect Norwegian and allied forces, critical societal functions, and critical functions for the Armed Forces GNF

[2084] The Ministry of Defence's activities, freedom of action and decision-making capacity

[2085] Cryptographic solutions are essential for the protection of classified information and communications

[2086] To maintain national control over high-grade crypto, expertise and technological development within cryptology must continue to be prioritized

[2087] In accordance with Norwegian crypto policy, and to follow up on the government's ambition to strengthen national crypto competence, the government will establish a national competence environment for applied cryptology in collaboration between the National Security Authority (NSM), industry and academia

[2088] The government will also strengthen NSM's crypto environment with expertise and high-tech equipment, including through an upgrade of NSM's crypto laboratory

[2089] In order to safeguard the defense sector's fundamental national functions, the Defense Forces' objects and infrastructure that are worthy of protection must be secured

[2090] The aim is to establish permanent ground protection for existing objects worthy of protection (as of December 2019) by the end of

[2091] The number and type of objects worthy of protection will change through annual review processes

[2092] In the new security law, infrastructure has been introduced as a new category of value that must be secured against security-threatening activities

[2093] Securing infrastructure, and any new objects that are designated as worthy of protection, must be safeguarded

[2094] People with access to sensitive assets may be recruited or pressured into cooperation by state intelligence services

[2095] An "insider" will be able to eliminate physical and digital security barriers that have been established

[2096] Good personnel security is an important and integrated part of the overall work on preventive security, and the government will consider in more detail how research-based knowledge about insider risk can be increased

[2097] In order for the work on security clearances and authorizations in the defense sector to maintain a high professional level, and for the sector's clearance authority to have satisfactory processing times for clearance cases, changes have already been made to the structure of the clearance authorities and to the regulations

[2098] NSM has been tasked with digitizing the processes related to security clearance and authorization, as well as automating case processing where possible

[2099] This will lead to faster case processing, better resource utilization, and better traceability and control, which could provide an increased degree of legal certainty and equal treatment

[2100] Digitalization will also help meet the government's goal of ensuring that conscripts are security cleared before reporting for duty

[2101] The challenges with today's manual handling of clearance and authorization apply not only to the defense sector, but also to civilian sectors

[2102] The measure will have significant effects both for the defense sector's central clearance authority in the Defense Security Department and for the Civilian Clearance Authority

[2103] Digitalization of processes during the long-term plan period will therefore be done jointly between the defense sector and civilian sectors

[2104] Today's complex threat and challenge picture, with the use of instruments that cross sectors and borders, affects all sectors of society

[2105] Events that are apparently aimed at public security objectives may in reality be designed to affect state security and our national security interests

[2106] Composite threats, composite use of instruments and hybrid

[2107] Threats are related and partly overlapping concepts

[2108] There is no uniform definition of compound threats, but the phenomenon involves the use of different means in combination to influence an adversary with the greatest possible effect

[2109] This can involve creating uncertainty, doubt and confusion, making decision-making processes difficult and influencing decisions in a direction that is favorable to the actor in question, including achieving strategic advantages that are traditionally achieved through victory in war

[2110] Individually, the various instruments can also pose a threat, for example to critical infrastructure, to information we want to protect, or to the pillars of our democracy

[2111] Examples include trust in authorities, trust between people and between groups of people, and free democratic debate

[2112] The use of instruments can be aimed at specific, time-limited activities or situations, or be more long-term in order to undermine trust and weaken the foundation on which liberal democracies are built

[2113] The means of influence can be diplomatic, military, informational, economic, intelligence and legal

[2114] When several instruments are used together, they can reinforce each other and increase the overall effect, creating challenges that are difficult to understand in scope and dilemmas that are difficult to handle

[2115] For example, a digital attack against critical infrastructure, such as a computer network, could be attempted combined with a disinformation campaign that Norwegian authorities are incapable of ensuring Norwegian citizens have safe access to the internet

[2116] Then the threats to our society are complex and affect across sectors

[2117] In this long-term plan for the defense sector, the term composite threats (and not hybrid threats) is used precisely to emphasize that both threats and the use of instruments can be composed of different components

[2118] Complex, cross-sectoral use of instruments blurs the distinction between peace and armed conflict, challenges across legal areas of responsibility, and exploits the other party's vulnerabilities and own capabilities

[2119] The use of a combination of instruments can occur in security policy gray areas, where the purpose is to create discord and destabilize

[2120] Such gray areas are below the thresholds traditionally associated with armed conflict

[2121] A gray zone situation will potentially be scaled up with the use of direct military force to achieve the desired effect on the adversary

[2122] Gray-zone situations challenge our understanding of state and societal security as two clearly distinct concepts

[2123] The recognition that the distinction between societal security and state security is being challenged is a prerequisite for strengthening society's ability to cope with the complex use of instruments

[2124] The challenges require a significant degree of cross-sectoral collaboration and a comprehensive understanding of the situation across sectors and levels

[2125] Today’s technological information carriers have radically expanded the scope for using well-known instruments in a way that makes society more exposed and more vulnerable to unwanted influence and influence than before

[2126] Information technology enables influence, intelligence gathering and surveillance, as well as attacks on infrastructure and assets on a scale, reach and speed that challenge our ability to detect and deal with this

[2127] The use of today's information technology can make it difficult to uncover the origin behind, for example, an initiated influence campaign or a digital attack

[2128] This concerns so-called attribution challenges

[2129] Norway must expect to be exposed to influence more frequently, through the use of instruments that appear both individually and in combinations

[2130] The origin behind such campaigns can be both state and non-state actors

[2131] Being prepared to handle the complexity of complex policy use requires awareness of how to protect our values

[2132] This is about the overall resilience of the state and society, the ability to withstand a societal shock or crisis, both in terms of handling the situation and the ability to resume normal societal functions as quickly as possible

[2133] The combined use of instruments places greater demands on national management with coordination across all sectors, particularly due to the uncertainty associated with attribution and intention

[2134] Total defense constitutes the framework for coordination of several sectors and is a good starting point for meeting complex threats

[2135] Many elements in a complex threat picture are largely met by parts of society other than the Armed Forces

[2136] On the civilian side, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, by virtue of its coordinating role within public security, is assigned the main responsibility for following up and coordinating the government's work related to issues of complex threats

[2137] The National Security Report has a more detailed description of the work against complex threats

[2138] The Armed Forces must have the ability to handle complex threats to its own sector, and also be able to contribute to broader management across sectors

[2139] This includes a particular need for enhanced ability to understand and manage threats in the digital space, and threats related to strategic communication and influence

[2140] The Armed Forces should also be able to exploit the potential inherent in the use of digital space and strategic communication

[2141] Strategic communication

[2142] Strategic communication, in a foreign and security policy context, can be described as a state or non-state actor's planned and coordinated use of all communicatively appropriate means to achieve its objectives vis-à-vis an adversary

[2143] The main purpose is to influence the perceptions, attitudes and behavior of target groups

[2144] Strategic communication encompasses a broad range of instruments, such as ordinary communication activities, diplomacy and information operations, including instruments such as disinformation and psychological operations

[2145] Military operations and activities also have a dimension of strategic communication associated with them

[2146] Strategic communication is used in both peacetime and conflict

[2147] A counterparty's use of strategic communication may be linked to specific events, but may also have a more long-term perspective to weaken a counterparty's stability, reputation and governance capabilities

[2148] The defense sector's understanding of strategic communication is consistent with NATO's definition

[2149] Developments in information technology have increased the potential to reach many actors both quickly and efficiently

[2150] This has given strategic communication a much greater scope for possibilities in terms of scope, speed and effect

[2151] Therefore, strategic communication has also become a central tool in the complex use of policy instruments

[2152] Strategic communication also has great relevance for military operations and military activity

[2153] The Armed Forces must have a conscious attitude towards the challenges associated with the information sphere and strategic communication

[2154] Overall, developments in strategic communication represent both challenges and opportunities

[2155] In order to ensure the best possible defense of Norway and Norwegian values, control over one's own information environment and the ability to defend against communication-related threats are required

[2156] Strategic communication can affect the Armed Forces' ability to carry out its tasks both directly and indirectly

[2157] An adversary may attempt to deter and demotivate defense personnel and other actors so that the Armed Forces' ability to execute is weakened

[2158] An adversary may also attempt to create general uncertainty, confusion and chaos in society, thereby weakening the authorities' decision-making ability

[2159] Truthful communication in word and deed is the guideline for the defense sector, and is an effective countermeasure if Norway is exposed to hostile disinformation

[2160] Disinformation, that is, deliberately misleading information to influence public debate or decision-making processes, or undermine democratic processes, is discussed in more detail in the societal security report

[2161] In order to counter and defend against hostile strategic communication, it is important to have a good situational picture and good situational understanding

[2162] The instruments used can affect both civilian and military sides, they can cross a number of sectoral boundaries and have a large scope

[2163] In addition, it can often be challenging to distinguish hostile strategic communication from ordinary communication activities

[2164] It is therefore crucial to put together a comprehensive situational picture in order to gain an overview of the challenges and be able to implement countermeasures

[2165] The defense sector must strengthen its ability to understand the situation regarding threats and challenges within strategic communication

[2166] At the same time, the defense sectors are completely dependent on good and well-developed cooperation with the civilian side in this field

[2167] Strengthening the defense sector's own capacities in this area must be combined and correspond with measures in other sectors of society

[2168] Raising awareness about the threat landscape in the information environment is a key tool for increasing resilience against influence

[2169] By increasing the understanding of how tools can be used communicatively, the ability to both uncover and resist attempts at hostile influence activity will improve

[2170] Awareness and professional support are therefore necessary for the Armed Forces to be able to meet this type of activity

[2171] During the long-term plan period, the Government will further develop and strengthen the expertise and professional environment surrounding strategic communication throughout the defense sector, and strengthen the environment for research and development in the field

[2172] This will also improve the Armed Forces' ability to utilize the potential of instruments that fall within the scope of strategic communication in military operations

[2173] To achieve this, arrangements must be made to strengthen subject areas and ensure close cooperation between strategic, operational and tactical levels in the defense sector

[2174] The integration of strategic communication into operational planning and operations will be further developed

[2175] This is supported by strengthening staff functions in the Armed Forces with personnel with relevant professional expertise

[2176] This involves both strengthening the resources to conduct open communication activities at all levels, and strengthening the ability to use information operations as an integrated part of military operations

[2177] This will also help improve our ability to interact with allies during exercises and operations, and to draw on the expertise of NATO and allied partners

[2178] Cooperation on dealing with threats in the digital space

[2179] The digital space provides threat actors with opportunities to commit data breaches, engage in espionage, sabotage, and conduct influence campaigns

[2180] This can happen across sectors, quickly and with potentially great impact

[2181] The responsibility for handling incidents and crises related to digital threats follows the same principles as for other crisis management

[2182] Maintaining digital security is primarily a business responsibility and business managers are responsible for conducting risk assessments and, based on this, implementing adequate measures

[2183] Each minister has overall responsibility for ensuring digital security in their own sector

[2184] Below is a more detailed description of some actors who have special responsibility in this field

[2185] Reference is also made to the civil security report for a description of civilian actors' areas of responsibility

[2186] Digital attacks are an increasingly important part of military operations

[2187] There is agreement within NATO that digital attacks can have just as serious consequences as attacks with conventional weapons, and that they are therefore covered by Article 5 of the Atlantic Treaty on collective defense

[2188] Most military operations today require access to the cyber domain and control of their own information infrastructure

[2189] The armed forces are increasingly dependent on civilian digital infrastructure to be able to carry out their tasks

[2190] It is essential for national security that civilian ICT systems that are critical for allied reception and the Armed Forces' operations do not fail

[2191] Freedom of action in the digital space to support military operations requires close cooperation across the civilian and military sectors, with an emphasis on improving civilian actors' own work with digital security

[2193] The National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) has been established as part of the NSM to improve and ensure a more coordinated national ability to deal with threats in the digital space

[2194] The center will ensure good utilization of society's overall resources in the area

[2195] The National Security Report has a more detailed discussion of the development of NSM

[2196] The cooperation between the Intelligence Service, NSM, the Police Security Service and Kripos within the framework of the Joint Cyber ​​Coordination Center (FCKS) will be continued

[2197] The cyber defense liaison at NCSC will continue and ensure information sharing between NCSC and milCERT

[2198] With the introduction of facilitated collection of cross-border electronic information as a result of the new Intelligence Services Act, the ability to detect, monitor, report on, handle and counter digital threats against Norway is strengthened

[2199] The defense sector's ability to prevent, detect and handle threats in the digital space must be strengthened to protect the Defense's own operations

[2200] The Armed Forces should also be able to contribute to better national situational awareness and contribute to national security related to threats in the digital space

[2201] Access to timely and relevant information about threats and threat actors is essential to being able to handle threats in the digital space

[2202] The Government will therefore further develop the Intelligence Service's ability in peace, crisis and armed conflict to monitor, attribute, warn and actively counter digital threats before incidents occur

[2203] Cyber defense is geared towards security monitoring and protection of the defense sector's own ICT systems, and has little capacity to assist in the protection of civilian ICT systems

[2205] The Ministry of Defense is responsible for digital security in the defense sector

[2225] At the NATO summit in Warsaw in 2016, Allies agreed on the so-called Cyber Defence Pledge

[2226] Through the declaration, Allied Heads of State and Government have committed to improving the ability to protect both civilian and military national ICT systems against digital attacks

[2227] Norway has been accepted as a member of the NATO-accredited Cooperative Cyber ​​Defence Centre of Excellence, in Estonia

[2228] The Norwegian participation is a collaboration between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, and the Ministry of Defense

[2229] The participation is part of the government's policy to promote civil-military and international cooperation on digital security and consensus on state behavior in the digital space

[2230] Comprehensive national situational awareness

[2231] The Government is continuously working to strengthen the ability to establish a comprehensive national situational awareness to better see threats and incidents in different sectors in context

[2232] Defense capability and effective resilience require the ability to understand a threat situation across sectors

[2233] Good situational awareness is essential for making good and timely decisions

[2234] Experience from exercises, especially after Trident Juncture 2018, shows that it can be challenging to establish a common civil-military understanding, assess expected developments and which measures should be implemented

[2235] Good situational awareness requires good and timely reporting and coordination mechanisms and routines, within and between different sectors, even though different actors have different needs for access to information

[2236] The government has initiated several measures to strengthen the ability to have a comprehensive understanding of the situation, including through strengthened dialogue between public authorities and private and semi-private enterprises

[2237] At the same time, there is a further need to strengthen the ability for cross-sectoral situational understanding and information flow both in normal situations and during crises

[2238] Faced with a complex threat landscape, enhanced situational awareness is a key prerequisite for improving the ability to make timely and precise decisions at all levels of government

[2239] Within this framework, another prerequisite is that relevant analytical expertise is further developed at various levels of administration, both to compile a situational picture and to be able to interpret and understand the situational picture

[2240] During the long-term plan period, the Government will assess how the respective civilian and military situational pictures can together improve the overall national situational understanding

[2241] The Armed Forces will contribute to a greater extent by sharing military situational awareness with more actors than today

[2242] Civilian and military situational awareness must be systematically exchanged and combined to provide a comprehensive national understanding

[2243] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will further develop the ability to establish, maintain and analyze a cross-sectoral situational picture at a strategic level on the civilian side

[2244] The Government has clarified responsibilities related to who is to compile information about various incidents that may be part of the complex use of policy instruments

[2245] In this work, the Police Security Service, the Intelligence Service and the National Security Authority have important roles

[2246] The Norwegian Police Directorate, the Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness and other relevant directorates and agencies must be actively involved

[2247] The cooperation between and the dissemination of information from the intelligence and security services (EOS services) has been strengthened over a number of years, but will be further developed as part of the work on improved national situational awareness

[2248] There is also a growing need for access to information about threats to critical societal functions and critical infrastructure

[2249] The provision of information from EOS services to actors responsible for security and preparedness will be further developed, partly as a necessary consequence of the fact that actors subject to the new Security Act need access to threat assessments and expertise of importance to the companies' preventive security work

[2250] This will primarily be based on already established cooperation arrangements

[2251] Among such cooperation arrangements is the Intelligence Service's cooperation with the Police Security Service in the Joint Counterterrorism Center (FKTS

[2252] The two services also collaborate with the National Security Authority and the Norwegian Criminal Police Office in the Joint Cyber Coordination Center (FCKS

[2253] FCKS and relevant partners from both the private and public sectors with responsibility for digital security are co-located with the National Cyber ​​Security Center (NCSC), which is part of the National Security Authority

[2255] Cross-sectoral collaboration for spatial situational awareness

[2258] In the worst case, the ability to safeguard national security interests could also be jeopardized, as both surveillance and military operations depend heavily on using satellites

[2259] Deliberate actions against satellite-based systems would pose a significant risk to the functioning of society and the operational capability of total defense

[2263] A strategy for Norwegian space activities) the government will strengthen Norwegian authorities' situational awareness in space through cross-sectoral cooperation

[2275] There is significant overlap between civilian, military and commercial interests

[2276] Common interests make Space Situational Awareness (SSA) an important area for pooling resources at the national level

[2278] In this context, the Norwegian Armed Forces shall contribute to the development and establishment of a national capability for SSA. The Total Defence Concept provides broad frameworks for civil-military cooperation. The Total Defence Concept provides the necessary flexibility and good resource utilisation by allowing both civilian and military resources to be used to solve challenges to both societal security and national security

[2279] It is about making the best possible use of available, but limited, resources and is therefore good social economics

[2280] The total defense concept provides a broad framework for civil-military cooperation, and is a good starting point for meeting complex threats, with a broad range of instruments

[2281] The arrangements within the total defence will be further developed to continue to be a relevant defence policy tool for responding to the security policy challenges Norway faces at any given time

[2282] The principle of responsibility is the underlying principle of total defense

[2283] The responsibility principle means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary incidents in the area

[2284] This means that responsibility is clearly placed in the various sectors

[2285] Incidents often affect businesses across sectors and the principle of cooperation should ensure necessary coordination between sectors

[2286] Effective collaboration requires continued efforts to develop good procedures, routines and a collaborative environment

[2287] Within the framework of the total defense concept, several formal and informal professional forums and civil-military cooperation bodies have been established, at central, regional and local levels

[2288] Most of these collaborative bodies are subject-specific and have their mandate within a smaller part of the total defence concept

[2289] Some examples are the Crisis Committee for Nuclear Emergency Response, the Emergency Response Committee against Biological Incidents, and the NORTRASHIP management

[2290] Overall, the bodies contribute to stronger institutionalization of the total defense concept

[2291] Civilian support to the Armed Forces Background for the Armed Forces' need for civilian support

[2292] In a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict, the Armed Forces' needs for goods, services, personnel and access to infrastructure will exceed what the Armed Forces have at their disposal

[2293] The total defense concept implies that this additional need must be covered by civil society, where a number of critical goods and services are partly based on imports and crossborder movement of labor

[2294] This development has certain vulnerabilities in terms of preparedness that require increased attention

[2295] For example, there will be a need for a certain proportion of national stocks and in-house production of particularly critical emergency goods

[2296] In addition, a national capability for critical service delivery may also be necessary

[2297] Norwegian and allied forces depend on civilian support to be able to carry out operations in Norway of a larger scope and longer duration

[2298] Civilian support for military forces is crucial to the country's defense capability

[2299] The Government will continue work on emergency plans and increased security of supply

[2300] Priority is given to measures to ensure civilian support in the form of fuel supply, transport services and health services, as well as basic services such as robust power supply and ICT

[2301] The national force structure and allied reinforcements must be supported simultaneously

[2302] A number of variables, such as the location and intensity of the conflict, as well as which allied reinforcements are involved, mean that requirements assessments are subject to some uncertainty

[2303] In addition to the support needs identified in advance, emphasis is placed on the fact that the civilian side must, as far as possible, also be able to support unforeseen military needs, if necessary by using requisition in a serious crisis situation

[2304] Revitalization of civilian support for the Armed Forces within the framework of total defense began with the revision of national defense plans

[2305] NATO updated its allied reinforcement and defense plans following Russia's annexation of Crimea

[2306] Exercise Trident Juncture 2018 contributed to increased attention to the High North within NATO

[2307] Norway demonstrated a credible ability to receive and support Allied reinforcements on a large scale

[2308] The experiences from the exercise contributed to the work of revitalizing total defense and identifying further areas of focus

[2309] Relevant civilian actors were involved in the planning at an early stage and contributed, among other things, to the development of a host country support concept for the Armed Forces

[2310] The plans that were prepared before the exercise and the experiences gained during the exercise mean that the Armed Forces are now better prepared to receive and support allied reinforcements

[2311] The extensive work that has been done in recent years to revitalize preparations for civilian support to the Armed Forces will continue during the long-term plan period

[2312] This is based on agreed and fundamental arrangements such as commercial agreements with contingency clauses and advance requisitions

[2313] Basic instruments** Civilian support to the Armed Forces is based on three basic instruments: Emergency preparedness legislation, cooperation and emergency preparedness bodies, and exercises

[2314] There are several laws that have preparedness as their purpose, including the Preparedness Act, the Requisition Act, the Health Preparedness Act, the Food Preparedness Act, the Ship Requisition Act, and the Defense Act

[2315] In addition, there are a number of other laws with emergency preparedness content, including the Aviation Act, the Railway Act, the Occupational Transport Act, the Electronic Communications Act, the Ports and Waterways Act, and the Energy Act, among others

[2316] Further work in this field involves, among other things, that the Armed Forces, in collaboration with responsible sector authorities, must conduct a review of relevant regulations with a view to whether they are still suitable for regulating support for the Armed Forces in crisis and armed conflict

[2317] There are around thirty cooperation and emergency preparedness bodies at a central level that can contribute to the work of supporting the Armed Forces

[2318] The most important in this context are the Central Total Defense Forum, the Health Preparedness Council, the Food Preparedness Council, the NORTRASHIP management, the Fuel Preparedness Council, the Power Supply Emergency Response Organization, the Advisory Forum for Civil Transport Preparedness, the Biological Incident Preparedness Committee, the Nuclear Preparedness Crisis Committee and the Electronic Communications Security Forum

[2319] The Government will further develop and facilitate effective interaction between the defense sector and the various civilian cooperation and emergency preparedness bodies in order to further develop total defense

[2320] In the years ahead, exercises will be a key tool in the further development of total defense

[2321] It is important that weaknesses identified during exercises are used systematically and actively

[2350] More about the war theater

[2351] In the Norwegian context, the declaration of a theater of war is used to regulate the relationship between civilian and military authorities

[2352] A theatre of war may be declared in that part or parts of the country where hostilities are taking place or may be presumed to be imminent, and where it is deemed necessary for the military authorities to take over the leadership of the police and other civilian administrative bodies in order to promote and secure military operations and supplies

[2353] The boundaries of the theater of war are normally determined by the King

[2354] The theater of war does not necessarily coincide with the military division of the area of operations

[2355] A theatre of war is automatically triggered where military forces are directly affected by hostilities. Civil-military cooperation and civil emergency preparedness have also received greater attention in NATO in recent years

[2356] Civil preparedness, crisis management and robust critical societal functions are a prerequisite for the individual country, and thus the alliance's overall preparedness, resilience and defence

[2357] Against this background, NATO decided in 2016 that allied nations should build increased resilience in civil society within a number of sector-specific areas, and specifically adopted "seven fundamental expectations" for member states' resilience in critical societal functions

[2358] The content has been subject to regular revisions and updates

[2359] At the NATO Defense Ministerial meeting in June 2020, these were updated to include, among other things, preliminary key lessons learned from the COVID-19 crisis, including the importance of robust supply chains, identification of critical personnel, and maintenance of basic societal functions

[2360] To follow up on NATO's seven fundamental expectations, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security established the same year

[2361] The Total Defense Program to further develop total defense and increase resilience in critical societal functions on the civilian side

[2362] The establishment of the Total Defence Programme since 2016 is considered to have been an important factor in the broader work to further develop and modernise total defence

[2363] The program has also contributed in several areas to the sectors' work to strengthen deliveries and robustness in critical societal functions and to the assessment of fundamental national functions

[2364] The program has contributed to increased knowledge and expertise about roles, responsibilities and authority related to security crises and armed conflict

[2365] Despite the fact that great progress has been made in the work of further developing total defense and increasing the resilience of critical societal functions on the civilian side, the work is a continuous process that must also continue after the Total Defense Program ends

[2366] The defense sector will be an active contributor to this work

[2367] Societal security affects the Armed Forces' ability to safeguard national security

[2368] If key infrastructure such as hospitals, electronic communications or electricity and power supplies are threatened or fail, this will have a major impact on the Armed Forces' operational capability

[2369] Strengthening the resilience of civil society, and the ability to coordinate across sectors, is of great importance for defense capability. International law of war and the use of civilians International law of war and national legislation, including guidelines from the Ministry of Defense and internal regulations in the Armed Forces, establish the legal framework for the use of military force in armed conflict

[2370] The international law of war only applies in armed conflict

[2371] The use of civilians to support military operations in armed conflict is, with limitations, permitted under the international law of war

[2372] The limitations of the international law of war must be respected

[2373] Planning for, and training in, civilian support in armed conflict must be in accordance with the international law of war

[2374] The international law of war is based on the principles of distinction between civilians and combatants, military necessity, humanity and proportionality

[2375] The principle of distinction implies that civilians should be protected from the dangers of military operations, and that attacks should only be directed against lawful military objectives

[2376] When providing civilian support for military operations, Norway's international law obligation to protect civilians from the dangers of military operations must be upheld

[2377] The principle of proportionality implies that civilians who are on or near military targets may legitimately suffer collateral damage from attacks on the military target

[2378] This is one of the dangers to civilians when supporting military operations

[2379] The obligation to protect civilians from the dangers of military operations means that the risk of collateral damage to civilians must be managed and kept low

[2380] Mechanisms for risk assessment of civil collateral damage must be established, which safeguard Norway's international law obligations

[2381] Civilians who participate directly in hostilities lose protection from attack and risk prosecution

[2382] The use of civilians in this way is contrary to the general obligation to protect civilians from the dangers of military operations

[2383] National regulations prohibit the defense sector from using civilians in functions that constitute direct participation

[2384] The agencies in the defense sector must identify these types of functions to be performed by combatants in armed conflict

[2385] Norway has a duty to assess whether new methods of warfare are in accordance with the international law of war

[2386] When developing concepts for civilian support, an international law assessment must be carried out to identify limitations in the international law of war and take these limitations into account in the design of the concepts

[2387] The use of civilians in support of military operations shall not impair the general protection of the civilian population in accordance with the principle of distinction

[2388] The opposing party should not have difficulty distinguishing between combatants and civilians, as this could ultimately deprive the opposing party of the incentive to comply with the distinction principle. One of the tasks of the Armed Forces is to contribute to safeguarding civil security and other key societal tasks (task no

[2389] Several departments in the Armed Forces have, as part of their overall mission portfolio, to carry out key societal tasks, such as the civilian tasks of the Coast Guard, the Border Guard, His Majesty the King's Guard and the Intelligence Service

[2391] This applies, for example, to natural disasters, epidemics, accidents and serious criminal acts such as terrorism

[2474] National Emergency Response System** The National Emergency Response System (NBS) is a cross-sectoral procedural and decision-making tool for central political authorities and individual agency heads in the event of a security crisis, armed conflict and other cross-sectoral crises caused by serious intentional acts

[2475] NBS is harmonized with NATO's emergency preparedness system, NATO's Crisis Response System (NCRS), to ensure rapid and coordinated decisions between Norway and NATO, but is adapted to national conditions and needs

[2476] The NBS consists of the Defence Sector Emergency Preparedness System (BFF) and the Civil Emergency Preparedness System (SBS

[2477] All sectors on the civilian side have a responsibility related to the National Emergency Preparedness System

[2478] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for coordinating SBS on the civilian side, while the Ministry of Defence is responsible for coordinating BFF in the defence sector

[2479] The Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security are jointly responsible for ensuring that BFF and SBS are harmonised and correspond with measures across sectors

[2480] NBS is a framework that requires the preparation of underlying plans in order to have value as a decision-making tool

[2481] All ministries and subordinate agencies and agencies designated by the ministries must prepare their own emergency plans based on the NBS

[2482] The NBS is subject to regular audits, led by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and the Ministry of Defense, to ensure that the measures are continuously quality assured and developed

[2483] The significant changes in the threat landscape mean that the government will carry out further impact assessments of the measures in the NBS during the long-term plan period to assess whether they are appropriate, feasible and realistic, and whether there are measures that are missing

[2484] The outbreak of the COVID-19 virus disease in the winter of 2020 has had significant consequences for most areas of Norwegian society, including the defense sector

[2485] It is too early to draw conclusions about what specific consequences the corona pandemic may entail in its full scope

[2486] An evaluation of the handling of the corona pandemic has been initiated in the defense sector

[2487] The purpose is to draw lessons from the handling of the crisis, and from its consequences for the defense sector, so that improvements can be made to ensure that the sector is best equipped to handle future crises

[2488] The defense sector's evaluation will also contribute to other evaluations of the pandemic, including the Corona Commission appointed by the government

[2489] The commission will map all relevant aspects of the national handling of the pandemic, and will submit its report in the spring

[2490] The pandemic's consequences for the security situation** In addition to the pandemic's serious direct consequences for the lives and health of citizens, it has also challenged the security situation of many countries in a broader perspective

[2491] Among other things, we have seen increased attention to security of supply of strategic goods and services, as well as more restrictions on cross-border interaction and increased protectionism

[2492] Increased nationalism and a lack of coordination of measures across borders can have consequences for relations between states and regions

[2493] The unpredictable dynamics of the pandemic have destabilizing potential, and in some areas appear to reinforce negative developments in international security that we have observed before the crisis

[2494] This includes increased great power rivalry, further pressure on international institutions and Western cooperation, and the broad use of instruments in international politics

[2495] We must take into account that some actors see increased security policy room for maneuver and are using the crisis to advance their goals and strengthen their position

[2496] The coronavirus pandemic is also a significant risk to public safety

[2497] The societal security report provides a thorough account of the handling of the corona pandemic in Norway and some of the vulnerabilities that the pandemic has revealed

[2498] The crisis has provided experience in handling cross-sectoral situations

[2499] The total defense concept encompasses civil-military cooperation across the entire crisis spectrum with the aim of utilizing our combined resources in the best possible way

[2500] The handling of the corona pandemic has shown that the total defense concept is also relevant in this type of crisis

[2501] Early in the corona pandemic, the Ministry of Defense gave the following three priorities for the Armed Forces, and the three other agencies in the defense sector

[2502] Maintain sharp missions, operational capability and readiness nationally and together with allies

[2503] Reduce the risk of infection in the sector's agencies and thereby also contribute to reducing the risk of infection in society in general

[2504] Take care of sick people in the agencies

[2505] Support civil authorities upon request

[2506] A number of measures have been implemented to meet these priorities

[2507] The Armed Forces have based their actions on the orders and guidelines set by national health authorities

[2508] In some areas, stricter infection control regulations have also been practiced than in society at large

[2509] The Armed Forces have maintained operational capability throughout the crisis

[2510] The Armed Forces have not had critical challenges in terms of the ability to maintain national military operations, international operations, emergency preparedness and other critical societal functions

[2511] The number of people in the Armed Forces who have been confirmed infected, and the number who have been in quarantine, has changed in line with the infection situation elsewhere in society

[2512] Although some departments have been somewhat reduced due to personnel in quarantine, this has not affected readiness times and the ability to build up forces if the situation required it

[2513] Restrictions due to Covid-19 have meant that assignments have been partially adjusted and sailing programs have been changed

[2514] It has also been necessary to reduce training activity both nationally and internationally

[2515] The major exercise "Cold Response 2020" was concluded at an early stage

[2516] In addition, the Home Guard canceled all training activities for a period of time, and some other national training activities were also affected

[2517] Norwegian participation in multinational exercises and international arms control activities has also been affected by the pandemic

[2518] Norwegian participation in military operations abroad has been continued

[2519] The outbreak of COVID-19 has led to varying degrees of restrictions on Norwegian troop contributions

[2520] The government, in consultation with our allies and coalition partners, has been assessing the situation on an ongoing basis

[2521] The measures deemed necessary have been implemented to safeguard the Norwegian forces

[2522] Replacement of conscripts, graduations and the like have largely been carried out according to original plans

[2523] Following dialogue between the Directorate of Health and the Armed Forces, the induction of new recruits has been carried out as planned, but with strict infection control regulations

[2524] A temporary law on the management of personnel in the Armed Forces came into force on April

[2525] The law provides authority to order civilian employees to other work tasks, as well as the ability to impose restrictions on freedom of travel and movement on both civilian and military employees in the Armed Forces

[2526] The purpose is to maintain operational capability and readiness

[2527] A regulation was established that granted the Armed Forces an exemption from the municipal quarantine regulations in order to transport personnel and equipment across municipal borders

[2528] The regulations, good dialogue at the local level and successive adjustments to the quarantine provisions solved the challenges with this

[2529] The coronavirus pandemic has shown society's dependence on electronic communication

[2530] The defense sector has also seen extensive use of home offices and video conferencing, which would not have been possible without well-functioning and secure electronic communications

[2531] The defense sector has a need for security-graded communication that must also be safeguarded in a situation such as the coronavirus pandemic

[2532] The pandemic has also shown the importance of national resources and emergency stocks

[2534] In other types of crises, there may be other goods that the Armed Forces depend on, such as fuel and ammunition

[2538] Throughout the crisis, mitigating measures have been implemented, including accelerating procurement and upgrading equipment

[2539] Furthermore, great emphasis has been placed on contributing to good dialogue and cooperation with other countries' authorities and industry to ensure the necessary maintenance of Norwegian suppliers' delivery obligations

[2555] The Armed Forces' most extensive contribution to civilian crisis management during the pandemic has not been directly health-related, but in the form of Home Guard assistance to police border control

[2557] In the period from March 14 to June 15, 2020, such assistance was provided by the Home Guard with a total of 1,063 personnel performing approximately 14,500 man-days
