[2565] A proposal for a statutory basis in the Defence Act regarding the Armed Forces' assistance to public authorities and other emergency response actors to safeguard public security has therefore been subject to general consultation

[2566] It will be relevant to follow up any new legal basis with a proposal for a regulation that will be a parallel to the instructions on the Armed Forces' assistance to the police. *** **8 International security and defense cooperation** The Government will strengthen and further develop efforts in the bilateral and multinational areas

[2567] Bilateral and multinational cooperation structures are becoming more important in a more demanding period for Norwegian security, where the challenges collectively exceed Norwegian capacity alone

[2568] The importance of supporting a rules-based world order and the Alliance's collective capabilities must be followed up with clearly prioritized cooperation with selected allies and partners, as well as regional security cooperation

[2569] As the government emphasized in the previous long-term plan, Norway must prioritize operational and security policy cooperation with selected allies that are relevant for bilateral and allied reinforcement of Norway in security policy crises and armed conflict

[2570] Cooperation with allies, also within the framework of NATO and other multinational forums, includes both deterrence and presence in daily operations, and in the defense of Norway in crises or armed conflict

[2571] In line with this, the protection of Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and freedom of action against political, military and other pressure will be the overarching guideline for the defense sector's international cooperation. **8.1 UN** The UN shall contribute to ensuring that states' conduct is based on international law and respect for human rights

[2849] Further development of the structure of the Armed Forces

[2850] A new security policy situation with a high rate of change is challenging our security

[2851] Long-range precision weapons, complex threats, increasingly rapid technological development and increased expectations of Norway

[2852] are factors that influence the need to further develop the structure of the Armed Forces

[2853] It must be taken into account that technology that can threaten the security of states is increasingly available to non-state actors

[2854] The Government will develop the defense structure in a way that facilitates further strengthening in upcoming long-term planning periods

[2855] The development of the Armed Forces shall build on the strategic choices made in the previous planning period, and the structure shall be sustainable in both the short and long term

[2856] Rapid technological development and more complex materiel and weapon systems increase the need for more flexible procurement schemes and a faster update cycle

[2857] This will help ensure that the Armed Forces' systems maintain their relative advantages and that the materiel and weapons systems are available throughout their service life

[2858] In the coming years, the Armed Forces will phase in a number of new capabilities and carry out several major upgrades to existing capabilities to ensure technical and operational relevance

[2859] The introduction of new material systems and updating of existing ones will, in the long term, strengthen the Armed Forces' operational capability and contribute to closing gaps in existing planning and in NATO's capability goals for Norway

[2860] Increased personnel volume will be prioritized and will gradually provide strengthened operational capability in all domains

[2861] In the long term, this will contribute to increased preparedness, responsiveness and endurance

[2862] The defense will be strengthened, and will be seen in the context of our bilateral reinforcement plans and relationships with close allies, in addition to our collective capability in NATO

[2863] Strengthening the Armed Forces' operational capability will therefore contribute to increasing the ability to receive reinforcements and deploy force contributions internationally

[2864] A more robust structure with greater impact will contribute to deterrence, increase the ability to resist, help protect transatlantic supply lines and thus better prepare the conditions for allied reinforcements to come to the rescue, if required

[2865] At the same time, the Armed Forces should be able to meet the needs and expectations of NATO and allies, and thereby contribute to a credible and balanced deterrence

[2866] In order to safeguard Norway's role as a stabilizing actor in the High North, sufficient situational awareness and presence must be prioritized

[3069] Box 9.1 Restoring capacity after the loss of KNM Helge Ingstad

[3070] The Norwegian Armed Forces' surface combat vessels currently consist of the Skjold-class corvettes and the Nansen-class frigates

[3071] Both corvettes and frigates have the ability to contribute to deterrence and can combat other surface vessels, and frigates also have a better ability to combat air and underwater threats than corvettes

[3072] The loss of KNM Helge Ingstad reduced the operational capacity of the Armed Forces

[3073] To reduce the operational consequences of the sinking in the short term, the crewing of the surface vessels in the Navy has been strengthened

[3074] In addition, the lost weapons and spare parts inventory is being restored

[3075] It is no longer possible to acquire a new frigate with the same design as the Nansen class, and it will be very resource-and expertise-intensive for the Armed Forces to operate two different frigate classes in parallel over an extended period of time

[3076] The government is therefore prioritizing upgrading the four remaining frigates

[3077] Among other things, the sensor and weapon systems will be modernized

[3078] This will help ensure that the frigates are relevant in the face of an increasingly challenging and complex threat landscape, and that the Nansen class can be operational until the mid-2030s

[3081] This vessel class is therefore not being phased out as originally planned

[3082] Overall, this will contribute to maintaining sufficient presence and operational capability in the Navy

[3175] The Home Guard (HV) shall contribute to the defense of Norway in peace, crisis and armed conflict by constituting the nationwide territorial land military component of joint operational and allied efforts

[3233] The service is subordinate to the Chief of Defence, but its work is not limited to military issues

[3234] The e-service's main mission is to warn of external threats to Norway and national security interests, support the Armed Forces, allies and partners, and support political decision-making processes with information of importance to Norwegian foreign, security and defense policy

[3235] The Head of the E-Service is responsible for the Armed Forces' cyber operations. Ambition and development The Government continues its commitment to the E-Service

[3236] Further development includes the E-service's ability to meet existing and new intelligence needs in line with geopolitical developments, changes in the threat landscape and technological developments in general

[3238] The threats in the digital space are often cross-sectoral

[3239] Network operations are characterized by being more coordinated and efficient than before

[3240] It is therefore important that the E-service keeps up with digital developments and is able to handle new threats

[3245] By being the best at maintaining the situational picture in its own local area, the E-service contributes to good decision-making processes and strong allied relationships

[3246] An important task in recent years has been to revise the legal basis for the Intelligence Service's activities

[3247] The Ministry of Defense submitted on April 22, 2020, Bill No

[3248] on a new Act on the Intelligence Service (Intelligence Service Act

[3249] The legislative proposal followed up on the Storting's request resolution no. 466 of 21 February 2017, in which the government was asked to submit a proposal for a revised Intelligence Services Act

[3250] The bill was passed by a broad majority in the Storting on June 15, 2020, and will enter into force on January

[3251] The new Intelligence Services Act facilitates further modernization of the service

[3252] The purpose of the law is to help secure Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity, democratic form of government and other national security interests

[3253] It helps to secure trust in and secure the basis for control over the E-service's activities, and ensure that the activities are carried out in accordance with human rights and other fundamental values in a democratic society

[3254] The law mainly codifies current regulations and practices, but also contains innovations

[3255] Among other things, rules are laid down regarding the facilitated collection of cross-border electronic communications to strengthen Norway's independent intelligence capabilities

[3256] The Act enables the E-Service to follow threat actors in the new technological reality, while safeguarding privacy and our democratic and constitutional values. [3322] A consequence of the new security policy situation is that the base structure with associated EBA infrastructure must be utilized to a greater extent as a strategic input factor

[3323] This implies a more flexible approach to the defense sector's EBA and entails the use of new cost-effective EBA solutions to strengthen preparedness and the ability to support operations in crisis and armed conflict

[3324] A high level of military activity, allied presence on bases, and the possibility of rapid allied reinforcement require access to the necessary EBA capabilities to facilitate rapid response and high readiness

[3325] Tightened readiness times and more material will require EBA that is adapted and balanced against these measures, and that can be made available at shorter notice than today

[3326] For the forces to be ready in a crisis or war situation, it is important to practice and train

[3327] Shooting and training ranges will therefore be further developed in the long term to support increased national needs, as well as to facilitate foreign units to practice and train together with Norwegian units to the greatest extent possible

[3328] To meet the need to establish and adapt the EBA more quickly than today, the strategic orientation of the defense sector's EBA will be adapted

[3329] The Ministry of Defense, in collaboration with the agencies, will develop an EBA strategy to contribute to better safeguarding the sector's primary objectives

[3330] The EBA strategy aims to create defensive capabilities through cost-effective and functional EBA services

[3331] This will include, among other things, a more flexible procurement solution, increased use of standardized solutions and semipermanent buildings, public and private collaboration, and increased use of rental markets and civil EBA where appropriate

[3334] New and existing EBA shall be further developed with more efficient management so that the current challenge of maintenance backlog and renewal is reduced within the current resource framework. [3420] The Norwegian Armed Forces, Defence Materiel (FMA), Defence Construction (FB) and the Defence Research Institute (FFI) are both administratively and professionally subordinate to the Ministry of Defence

[3423] The Armed Forces are the state's foremost instrument for safeguarding Norway's security against external threats

[3424] Other agencies shall support the Armed Forces so that tasks can be solved in the most efficient way possible, and act as advisors to the Ministry of Defence within their own areas

[3427] Defence equipment and Defence Buildings will continue to be further developed

[3533] for further information on the further development of cryptographic expertise and technology. **11 The Armed Forces as a social actor** **11.1 The defence sector's contribution to achieving the UN's Sustainable Development Goals** The defence sector shall contribute to Norway's efforts to achieve the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[3534] The UN goals are important for the sector, especially because one of the consequences of the world not achieving the goals is an increased risk of armed conflict

[3535] Contributing to the work to achieve the sustainability goals is a prioritized and natural part of fulfilling the Norwegian Armed Forces' social responsibility

[3536] The military is a major user of nature and the environment, and its activities leave their mark on land, in the air and at sea

[3537] It is therefore important that the sector implements targeted measures that reduce environmental impact

[3538] This is done through, among other things, environmental requirements for property, buildings and structures (EBA), such as energy efficiency

[3539] The Armed Forces impose requirements on suppliers of EBA and materiel so that the environmental and climate footprint is as small as possible

[3540] Another requirement is that the regulations for ethical and social trade are followed up

[3541] This includes requirements that employees have proper working conditions, a ban on child labor, and that suppliers have their own ethical guidelines

[3542] The Armed Forces' contribution to international security through participation in peacekeeping operations and other international military efforts helps to ensure fundamental human rights and economic progress

[3543] Through integrity building and anti-corruption work, the defense sector will contribute to better governance at home and abroad

[3544] This is done through preventive work, by setting requirements for our own sector and suppliers, and by collaborating with allies and partners

[3545] Further development and strengthening of institutions and capacity building nationally and internationally contributes to making it easier for everyone to achieve the sustainability goals

[3546] The sector has increased its efforts to promote diversity and equality

[3547] Several measures have been implemented to reduce bullying and harassment

[3548] The Ministry of Defence will set clear goals to improve gender equality and seek to increase diversity

[3549] The defense sector currently supports the UN's Sustainable Development Goals in several areas, and will strengthen its efforts, among other things, by integrating sustainability assessments into the general planning and management of the sector through targeted and strategic work

[3550] The defense sector's climate responsibility

[3551] The defense sector's direct climate emissions account for about 0.5 percent of total emissions in Norway (2018 figures

[3552] Based on a forecast from the defense sector's environmental database, greenhouse gas emissions from the Defense Department's activities will increase slightly over the next five years and will exceed 300,000 tons of CO2 equivalents in the years

[3553] The projection is an estimate based on general data, expected changes in the material structure and overall activity level objectives

[3554] It includes aircraft, vessels, vehicles, local energy production and purchased electricity and district heating

[3555] A number of targeted measures have been implemented to reduce both direct and indirect emissions from the sector, such as phasing out fossil oil for heating and energy-saving measures in buildings

[3556] The largest sources of greenhouse gas emissions in the sector are vessels and aircraft, which account for more than 85 percent of the sector's total emissions

[3557] In light of the overall goals for the defense sector, the Armed Forces must use the vessels and aircraft in which it has already invested

[3558] At the same time, it is important to look more closely at how the sector can best reduce direct and indirect emissions in the future, without compromising operational capability

[3559] The Armed Forces' environmental challenges are particularly related to the use of equipment, which when used in operations, exercises and training can cause adverse environmental impacts, including emissions in the form of noise

[3560] Environmental protection work in the defense sector includes both prevention of pollution and cleanup after previous pollution

[3561] Stress cannot be completely avoided, but it is important to minimize the stress through environmentally conscious planning and implementation of activities

[3562] The defense sector has a social responsibility for managing society's assets

[3563] This applies both through sustainable management of natural and cultural values on one's own property and through taking natural and cultural values into account during exercises and training

[3600] The defense sector is a significant steward of Norwegian cultural heritage and cultural environment and produces a diversity of cultural experiences

[3601] Cultural activities contribute to the follow-up of the UN's Sustainable Development Goal number 11, Sustainable Cities and Communities

[3602] Culture and tradition are closely linked to the operational activities of the Armed Forces and are an integral part of the defense sector's activities in general

[3603] The activities include building professional identity, knowledge development and veterans' policy

[3604] The quality of cultural activities in the Armed Forces affects the Armed Forces' reputation in general

[3605] Cultural activities in the defense sector are a link to society

[3606] It contributes to anchoring in the population by creating experiences and disseminating knowledge both internally and to society at large

[3607] There is great interest in and an influx of visitors to both national fortifications, the Armed Forces' museums and the Armed Forces' music events

[3608] Cultural activities attract great commitment in the form of associations of friends and volunteers who support cultural activities

[3609] Cultural activities require attention on their own terms, as they may be based on different guidelines, quality requirements and opportunities than other activities in the defense sector

[3610] At the same time, there is close cooperation and mutual dependence between culture and other defense activities

[3611] Culture must therefore be viewed both separately and together with other defense activities

[3612] The Government will seek to safeguard cultural activities in the defense sector and will emphasize, among other things, the preservation of expertise, the management of museum objects, and interaction between various cultural actors

[3613] The Government will see the further development of museum activities in the defense sector in connection with the Ministry of Culture's planned report to the Storting on the museum sector

[3618] The defense sector's contribution to value creation and jobs

[3619] Significant funds are allocated each year to protect and safeguard Norway's security, interests and values

[3620] The funds allocated are used for a wide range of areas, from the purchase of modern weapons systems, to salary payments to employees and investment in and maintenance of buildings

[3621] The use of the funds, in the form of businesses in the sector's purchases of goods and services, and employees' personal consumption, has a major economic effect

[3622] This applies primarily to those places where the defense sector is located, but also elsewhere in the country

[3623] The economic effect of the defense sector's activity and presence is estimated at approximately NOK 37 billion for the year

[3624] The economic impact from abroad through industrial agreements with civilian companies is additional

[3625] Wage payments to the sector's employees and the sector's purchases of goods and services were the largest sources of the economic impact

[3626] Furthermore, the economic effect was greatest in the following five counties

[3627] Oslo, Trøndelag, Akershus, Troms and Nordland (note that the county division here is used as it was in

[3628] These are counties with a high military presence and associated spillover effects for local communities

[3629] Support for volunteer work

[3630] The Ministry of Defence provides support to a number of voluntary organisations and other non-public actors that contribute to strengthening the population's knowledge and understanding of Norwegian defence and security policy, or that otherwise contribute to supporting the Defence Forces' goals and priorities

[3631] The voluntary organizations that receive support make significant contributions to the Armed Forces and the defense cause, and contribute to the Armed Forces' anchoring in society

[3632] The government wants to continue supporting volunteer work, but too close ties should not develop between volunteering and government activities

[3633] The government's declaration on volunteerism from 2015 recognizes the voluntary sector as an independent and necessary actor in Norwegian society

[3634] The declaration defines a framework for the interaction between the state and voluntary organizations

[3635] This establishes that the government does not want to regulate volunteering, but should support the uniqueness and driving force of volunteering by providing room for action, predictability, and facilitating growth from below

[3636] In 2020, the Ministry of Defence revised the current grant schemes and set them out in new regulations with the aim of simplifying grant management and providing better predictability in the coming period

[3637] The Ministry of Defence will continue its work to further develop the grant schemes and use the overall objectives set out in the voluntary declaration as guidelines

[3638] Implementation and management 2021–

[3639] This long-term plan facilitates the further development of a sustainable defense structure so that the Armed Forces can fulfill its tasks within the specified level of ambition in the short and long term

[3640] Norwegian security and defense policy aims to protect Norwegian sovereignty, territorial integrity, our democratic system of governance and our freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[3641] This is the defense sector's overall societal goal, and the basis for the approach to exercising governance in the sector

[3642] The government's defense policy is related to how the Armed Forces, NATO, cooperation with close allies, supported by total defense, are best used overall in the defense of the country

[3643] The objectives and framework set out in the defence policy shall support the realisation of the societal goal

[3644] The goals that the organizations in the defense sector will achieve will be based on the combination of accepted risk level, defense capability, and resources that best facilitates the achievement of the sector's societal goals

[3645] The entirety of the goals for the sector, and the measures the government proposes in this proposal, constitute a foundation for continued strengthening and further development of the defense sector, so that the Armed Forces remain a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[3646] It is desirable to manage underlying activities more generally and to a greater extent follow up on results and effects, and to a lesser extent resources and activities

[3647] This will facilitate giving agency heads greater freedom and responsibility for how goals are achieved

[3648] At the same time, it is a requirement that state funds are used efficiently, assets are managed in a responsible manner, and that the Storting's decisions and assumptions are followed up

[3649] A prerequisite for success with such a shift in management is that the agencies have good corporate governance

[3650] This includes the ability to develop the business through good goals and innovation, but also through internal governance, risk management, control and follow-up

[3651] Another prerequisite is that there is openness in the dialogue between the businesses and the ministry and that there is transparency in business management

[3652] A more results- and impact-based management must be founded on a high degree of trust in leaders of underlying organizations when it comes to implementing defense policy

[3655] In addition, the government annually presents its assessment of the Armed Forces' operational capability to the Storting

[3740] Priorities in implementation

[3741] The major changes that the defense sector has undergone, and which will continue in the coming four-year period, are very demanding to absorb for an organization that simultaneously has a number of daily, operational deliveries

[3742] If the goals set for this long-term plan period are to be achieved, it is important that changing conditions are handled on an ongoing basis, so that they are not postponed and accumulated, thereby undermining the possibility of realizing the goals

[3743] Timely realization of efficiency goals, and handling any currency fluctuations and changing fuel prices, are examples of challenges that must be taken into account in management and budgeting in order to realize the ambitions in this long-term plan

[3744] Many of the measures have mutual dependencies, are sequential and affect across businesses in the sector

[3745] Identified risks in the implementation will be continuously followed up with risk-reducing measures that will be decided at an appropriate level and communicated clearly at all levels of the organization

[3746] Holistic, long-term and predictable management in the defense sector is demanding, but of great importance, especially due to the long lead times associated with the development of operational capability

[3747] Long-term perspective and continuity are crucial for sufficient implementation capacity, and for being able to assess goal achievement and effects over time

[3748] The realization of the objectives depends on a number of internal and external conditions, which experience has shown may create challenges in implementation, and thus also for the long-term balance between tasks, structure and finances

[3749] Previously decided measures within the operational structure and the base and support structure that are being implemented will gradually produce economic effects in the coming period, and it is crucial that the defense sector is able to implement the structural measures in a timely manner to free up resources as expected

[3750] The release of resources from structural changes and efficiency improvements will help finance increased spending on strengthening selected areas

[3751] The goal set for resource release is ambitious, but realistic

[3752] Timely realization of efficiency gains is a prerequisite for achieving the goals in the long-term plan, and failure to achieve goals will thus have consequences that must be handled with mitigating measures or adjusted ambitions

[3753] The Armed Forces and the other organizations in the sector must continuously be able to fulfill their tasks within the stated ambition, while at the same time realizing the development measures that follow from this proposition

[3754] These considerations collectively set the framework for the implementation of this long-term plan and the management of the agencies in the defense sector during the period

[3755] Adequate and balanced consideration of both considerations must be emphasized by all businesses in the sector

[3756] In the period 2021–2024, the Government will give particular priority to following up on the measures initiated in the previous long-term plan, and to begin a gradual increase in the personnel volume for selected capacities

[3757] This includes, among other things, the completion of the fighter aircraft procurement and the acquisition of new maritime patrol aircraft

[3758] The catch-up on maintenance, spare parts and emergency stocks continues and supply readiness is being strengthened for all material classes

[3759] The establishment and commissioning of new departments continues and is being completed

[3760] For selected departments, the government will gradually increase the personnel volume with both permanent employees, conscripts in their first-time service, and reservists

[3761] Basic training for soldiers is being moved out of operational departments and concentrated at KNM Harald Haarfagre and Terningmoen

[3762] The effect of the measures will contribute to continued improvement in availability and resilience, including better facilitating the handling of concurrency challenges

[3763] New knowledge and experience have in some areas made it necessary to reassess certain assumptions that formed the basis of the previous long-term plan

[3764] The Norwegian krone has weakened over time against relevant foreign currencies

[3765] Within the significant increase in the defense framework proposed by the government, it has therefore been necessary to find room to finance the fact that operations in some areas have become more expensive than previously anticipated

[3766] This, also seen in the context of the general room for maneuver in the Norwegian economy, means that further renewal of equipment, expansion of existing departments, establishment of new departments and further increase in personnel volume will occur from 2025 onwards

[3767] However, in the planning period 2021–2024, the government will submit proposals for new material investments where the expenses primarily occur

[3768] Examples of such acquisitions are new tanks, long-range precision fire, new vessels for the Navy and Coast Guard, unmanned and autonomous systems, upgrading air defense capabilities, and replacing the Bell 412 helicopters

[3769] In order to achieve the highest possible utilization of resources, the Chief of Defence, in close collaboration with other heads of agencies, will be given room to maneuver to find the solutions that provide the best implementation

[3770] This applies, for example, to the order of the measures

[3771] Planning and implementation take place in close dialogue with the Ministry of Defence, within the annual budget framework and set against the security and defence policy framework and guidelines described in Chapter 2, as well as the financial conditions and framework described in Chapter 4 and the operational ambition described in Chapter

[3772] Overall control arrangement

[3773] This proposition forms the basis for the further development and management of the defense sector as a whole

[3774] Based on the sector's social goals, there are three main areas that contribute to goal achievement

[3775] The national capability of the armed forces, our collective capability in NATO and our bilateral plans for support and reinforcement from close allies, supported by the total defense

[3776] The following will guide the organization of the management of the defense sector

[3777] – Goals, frameworks and the management of the sector shall be based on the overall societal goal – Management shall actively engage with everyone who contributes to achieving the sector's societal and impact goals – Management shall be based on trust, uniqueness, risk and materiality

[3778] – Management should be simplified and made less resource-intensive

[3779] A holistic approach to management also includes assessment of achieved results

[3780] Appropriately designed performance measurement and evaluations make important contributions to learning, development and improvement throughout the sector, and to the work on further developing defense policy

[3781] Good systems for reporting and follow-up are also an important foundation for the sector's legitimacy in society

[3782] Emphasis on societal goals and effects The societal goals and effects are the starting point for the strategic management of the sector

[3783] Detailed monitoring of input factors and activity levels narrows the agencies' degree of freedom and room for maneuver

[3784] This reduces the incentive and commitment of businesses to facilitate the effective realization of their goals

[3785] By shifting management more towards the sector's societal goals and effects, efforts will be made to facilitate increased implementation capacity in the sector, and to make the sector more impact and results-oriented

[3786] Clear goals, based on clear priorities, provide underlying agencies with a good basis for achieving the overall societal goals and effects

[3787] Through management, freedom of action will be facilitated within the established and overarching goals and financial framework

[3788] A unified and comprehensive defense sector In the coordinated management of the sector, the Ministry of Defense will emphasize the importance of the agencies collectively aligning themselves towards realizing the sector's societal goals, and having good, effective and timely interaction based on the agencies' various missions, roles, authority and responsibilities

[3789] Support from civilian sectors is crucial for the country's defense capability, and thus also for achieving the sector's societal goals and impacts

[3790] The total defense concept encompasses mutual civil-military support across the entire crisis spectrum, and is about making the best possible use of available, but limited, resources

[3791] The Government will further develop the arrangements within the total defence concept to ensure that society's overall resources are utilized effectively to handle challenges to both state and societal security

[3792] Bilateral and multinational cooperation at various levels is crucial for the defense sector to achieve its societal goals

[3793] The international security community will be emphasized in the work on a more holistic perspective on governance in, and further development of, the defense sector

[3794] Management and follow-up based on trust, uniqueness, risk and materiality In order to fulfill their social responsibility, organizations in the defense sector must carry out their missions and manage their resources in a way that creates trust, support and legitimacy among the population as well

[3795] This assumes that the sector reflects society's norms, values and expectations, and complies with them

[3796] The ability to document the effects that have been achieved and how community resources have been used is also important for legitimacy

[3797] Emphasis will be placed on giving agencies in the defense sector freedom of action in the assignment solution

[3798] Management by objectives and results and trust-based management and leadership are based on the same assumptions

[3799] Goals, performance requirements and performance indicators will be followed up, and the agencies should have considerable freedom of action to choose how the goals and results are achieved

[3800] This implies a continued development towards less instruction-based and more clearly intention-based management in the defense sector

[3801] The balance point will not be constant over time, but is assessed and adjusted based on various factors and conditions, both internal and external

[3802] Management and follow-up will be adapted to the specific nature, risk and materiality of the activities

[3803] The specific structure of the management will therefore vary between and across different agencies and different fields and areas

[3804] Trust in the management relationship requires good understanding of roles, openness in dialogue and transparency based on a clear division of roles and responsibilities that is also sufficiently dynamic over time

[3805] Emphasis on the societal goal and greater freedom of choice in the assignment solution for agencies in the sector must be combined with a common understanding of the type and amount of management information needed, and how much should be documented

[3806] The agencies must have the ability to analyze and communicate effects and results so that they underpin a good management basis

[3807] Reporting in the defense sector shall primarily be facilitated to contribute to the further development of defense policy and activities in the sector

[3808] The reporting will also contribute to transparency and documentation

[3809] Simplified management and efficient use of resources

[3810] Holistic, predictable and long-term management is of great importance for achieving desired effects and achieving the sector's goals

[3811] Through clear goals and priorities, management will be simplified and made more efficient

[3812] By having the societal goal and effects as a starting point, priorities in follow-up can be more easily directed towards the most significant conditions

[3813] Management should be simplified, streamlined and have a defined purpose

[3814] This applies both to the alignment of goals and guidelines in management, and to follow-up through reporting, documentation and control

[3815] This will provide insight into important areas, including assessing whether goals and effects are achieved in a cost-effective and purpose-effective manner, and thus also provide a basis for prioritizing the overall resource effort in the sector

[3816] Emphasis will be placed on making the follow-up of the activities predictable, including by linking management and budget allocations to overall plans and long-term goals

[3817] By delegating authority to the level that knows the challenge best, management can facilitate more effective and targeted use of instruments

[3818] Continued development and effective utilization of digital tools, with increased access to information and new work processes and solutions, are important in this context

[3819] Digitalization will be essential to facilitate simplified management and efficient use of resources

[3820] This potential must be exploited without roles becoming ambiguous and formal responsibilities unclear

[3821] The government has committed to following up on the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[3822] Businesses in the sector will work purposefully and strategically with sustainability in planning and management to build on the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[3824] Strategic management of ICT activities in the defense sector

[3825] Modern ICT solutions are necessary to support operational capability and for the efficient implementation of activities in the defense sector

[3826] During this long-term planning period, the defense sector must strengthen its ability to adopt and utilize new technology quickly and effectively

[3827] Businesses in the sector should interact better with the civilian market and adopt new modern platforms and methods to establish and further develop ICT solutions

[3828] Businesses in the sector must ensure that necessary security is built into ICT solutions from the start and maintained continuously throughout their lifecycle

[3829] This will be a necessary basis for implementing the digitalization strategy of the defense sector, which will contribute to increased operational capability and increased efficiency

[3830] An ICT strategy was prepared in March 2019 and is now being implemented

[3831] The defense sector must have a forward-looking and innovative ICT operation that is coordinated and delegated, with the ability to utilize new platforms

[3832] The goal of the strategy is for the defense sector as a whole to utilize ICT as effectively as possible and in a way that better supports innovation

[3833] Responsibility should be delegated to the agencies within the framework of a clear and comprehensive management model, in line with the political framework and guidelines that have been provided

[3834] Central to the realization of the ICT strategy will be the work of developing and implementing a new ICT management model for the defense sector

[3835] In 2021, the intention is to transfer the responsibility, authority and function for exercising and further developing the strategic ICT management in the sector to the Chief of Defence

[3836] Adjustment of the budget chapter structure under the Ministry of Defence In line with the government's ambitions for simplified management and efficient use of resources, the government has, as discussed in the budget proposal for 2021, proposed changes to the budget chapter structure under the Ministry of Defence

[3837] In the budget chapter structure of the defense budget, the agencies, with the exception of the Armed Forces, have each had their own budget chapter, with one operating item and necessary investment items

[3838] For the Armed Forces, the allocation as of 2020 is divided into nine budget chapters with associated items, including eight ordinary operating items, one special operating item and two grant items

[3839] This limits the Chief of Defence's ability to reallocate budgetary funds in the implementation of the activity

[3840] The proposed changes will bring together the largest part of the Armed Forces' departments under one budget chapter

[3841] A less divided budget chapter structure will contribute to a more efficient implementation of the budget work and reduce the number of transactions in the revised national budget and the new balance

[3842] It will facilitate better governance of the sector and build on the government's goal of simplification and debureaucratization

[3843] At the same time, a collection of the Armed Forces' allocations into fewer chapters and items will better facilitate financial systems and processes in accordance with the financial regulations in the state

[3844] The change will strengthen the Chief of Defence's ability and capacity to more quickly follow up on the guidance of the Storting and the Government through reallocations between different purposes

[3845] Another factor that argues for fewer chapters is economic preparedness in times of crisis or armed conflict

[3846] With the proposed merger of budget chapters, the Chief of Defence will be able to reallocate funds between different parts of the Defence Forces in the event of acute needs that arise

[3847] The Government is concerned that the Storting is provided with sufficient information about how appropriations for military purposes are used

[3848] The Government therefore assumes that a reduced number of budget chapters should not reduce or weaken the information provided to the Storting about the various purposes of the Armed Forces' departments and how these are planned to be financed

[3849] A changed budget chapter structure will not reduce the Storting's ability to provide guidance for the defense budget

[3859] Rescue Helicopter Service The long-term development of the defense sector

[3860] The security situation for Norway has become more demanding than was the basis for Prop

[3861] Challenges and uncertainty are increasing as a result of global power shifts, great power rivalry, clearer security policy dividing lines within Europe and across the Atlantic, and the emergence of new domains for warfare

[3862] The situation with COVID-19 is also a reminder of the social and political challenges that can result from global crises such as worldwide pandemics

[3863] State security is being challenged more broadly through more complex use of instruments, and the West's technological lead is decreasing

[3864] Both state and non-state actors gain access to new technology with increased speed, power, and range

[3865] The distinction between peace and conflict, and between conventional and irregular warfare, is becoming less clear

[3866] Norway must take into account that a high rate of change, increasing unpredictability and greater complexity will also characterize developments beyond the period 2021–

[3867] Investment in defense and security is necessary for Norway's ability to resist pressure, threats, and attacks

[3868] Norwegian independence, sovereignty and freedom of action must be defended even in peace

[3869] The most important thing Norway does is contribute to stability and to avoiding armed conflict by demonstrating sufficient defense capabilities

[3870] Defense capability is built over time, based on the Armed Forces' own capabilities, NATO's collective defense and reinforcements from close allies, supported by a modern and prepared total defense

[3871] In the face of a more serious security situation, it is the sum of these capabilities that can deter attacks on Norwegian sovereignty, territorial integrity, our democratic governance and freedom of action

[3872] This, together with other calming measures, should promote predictability and stability in our local areas

[3873] Principles for long-term development of the defense sector

[3874] Long-term development of a relevant defense requires a combination of predictability and flexibility

[3875] It is crucial to create predictability around the organization's overall political goals and framework

[3876] It takes time to further develop the Armed Forces' capabilities and capacities, while at the same time the Armed Forces must have the necessary flexibility to handle new challenges

[3877] The armed forces' capabilities and capacities must be constantly adapted to meet changing threats and challenges, as well as to be able to operate together with allies

[3878] The Government bases the development of the defense sector on the principles of balance, realism and long-termism within a conceptual framework

[3879] Ensuring a balance within the Armed Forces so that the various structural elements provide a mutually reinforcing effect is necessary to achieve the greatest possible defense capability within the current financial framework

[3880] Development of military capability

[3881] The acquisition of operational military capabilities requires planning over a time horizon of several decades

[3882] As we have seen in recent years, the security situation can change rapidly

[3883] It must therefore be taken into account that the need for material, ICT and expertise necessary to achieve relevant and sufficient operational capability could change significantly within a ten-year period

[3884] At the same time, technological developments could provide completely new opportunities for building operational capabilities and carrying out operations

[3885] The military must be able to adopt new technology more quickly

[3886] Defence Equipment must contribute to reducing the time it takes to procure new equipment, and Defence Construction must do the same to procure properties, buildings and facilities

[3887] Procurement of military equipment will preferably be done as the acquisition of fully developed and commercially available equipment

[3888] For specially selected military capabilities, consideration will be given to developing our own solutions, but primarily together with allies to facilitate cooperation in operations and to achieve cost reduction

[3889] Volume and vulnerability

[3890] New operational capabilities will usually have different characteristics and better performance than the equipment they replace

[3891] The need for constant efficiency improvements also leads to increased unit costs

[3892] Reductions in volume and streamlining of operations have been used as means to cover the discrepancy between the expected and actual costs for different capacities

[3893] Although the operational effect on individual systems increases, a reduced volume in many cases leads to reduced endurance and flexibility, in addition to increased vulnerability

[3894] This is a development that could reduce the Armed Forces' overall operational capability, and over time increases the risk that necessary capacities will not be available when and where they are needed

[3895] As already announced in the St.prop

[3896] No. 48 (2007–

[3897] Within the limited resource framework of the defense sector, it will be neither possible nor desirable to drive continuous development, growth and renewal within all capacity areas in parallel

[3898] The challenge is intensified as digital space, outer space and the electromagnetic spectrum increase the Armed Forces' need for new capabilities

[3899] This situation will persist despite significant budget growth in the defense sector over recent years, and will challenge traditional thinking about renewing existing capabilities

[3900] It will be necessary to prioritize across capacities and domains, based on what best facilitates maintaining and further developing relative operational capability over time

[3901] This must also be seen in the context of what can be expected from support from NATO forces and allies in the future, through a holistic approach to the development of the Armed Forces' activities

[3902] The Armed Forces shall prioritize capabilities that provide the greatest possible national operational capability, and which at the same time constitute relevant contributions to NATO's collective defense

[3903] Holistic business development of the defense sector

[3904] In a modern defense, defense capability consists of more than the sum of the capacities of the individual elements

[3905] It is necessary to rethink how to build the delivery models that provide the greatest effect in the face of a new and complex threat landscape

[3906] The sector must adapt to available resources, see the new opportunities that both technological and societal developments provide, and find new ways around the limitations

[3907] This will help create a defense capability that meets the security situation to the greatest extent possible

[3908] This requires an open and more holistic approach to business development in the defense sector going forward

[3909] It will be essential to move towards more active processes where the emphasis is on the effects one wants to achieve, rather than exclusively emphasizing the input factors

[3910] The composition of the structure that constitutes a relevant defense depends on a number of factors that are constantly changing, and must be considered regardless of the relative size of the defense branches

[3911] This can provide new insights into how the sector as a whole should be organized, how processes should be designed, and what opportunities technology offers

[3912] In a material- and expertise-intensive sector with a long investment horizon and equipment lifespan, such a turnaround would not be possible or appropriate without taking into account the current structure and organization

[3913] Given a more challenging security policy situation, it is nevertheless necessary to begin work on shifting attention from material and structuredriven business development towards a more effects-based approach

[3914] Further improvement and efficiency enhancement

[3915] As part of the work on this long-term plan, FFI has pointed to a possible potential for benefit realization of between NOK 1.6 and 3 billion by 2024 within 28 benefit areas

[3916] The work of realizing the gains will require investments in, among other things, technology and expertise, in addition to restructuring several of the heavy processes in the sector

[3917] The introduction of good digital tools that provide a relevant data basis across the structures in the sector will also have an increased effect

[3918] The work on benefit realization and efficiency improvement is an important prerequisite for the realization of future long-term plans

[3919] At the same time, for the long-term development of the sector, it will also be necessary to think in new ways within efficiency

[3920] The challenges, and the need for more holistic business development, will also have implications and create opportunities within this area

[3921] Despite a number of restructuring and efficiency processes in recent decades, and an increasingly digitalized and professionalized defense, the sector has retained its delivery model based on autonomous operating units and defense branches with associated command structures and duplicative functions

[3922] The span of control of today's force commanders is still large, while societal developments point towards more robust organization based on the functional principle

[3923] The security situation and technological developments both create needs and provide opportunities for more integrated models for mission solutions

[3924] A review of the areas of force production, operational leadership, staff and command structure could potentially free up significant resources for increased operational effectiveness

[3925] Civil-military cooperation Civil-military cooperation has an important role in the defense of Norway, both through the defense sector's support for other sectors, civilian sectors' support for the Armed Forces, and when receiving allied forces

[3926] Increasing complexity in the threat landscape and the Armed Forces' increasing dependence on civilian support require that civil-military cooperation be developed holistically

[3927] The escalation period from the use of one instrument to a comprehensive use of instruments that threatens state security can be very short

[3928] This requires the ability to more quickly apply the nation's combined instruments so that effective countermeasures can meet developments in a timely manner

[3929] Cooperation on the development of civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defense will be necessary for the long-term development of Norway's security

[3930] The work on this long-term plan has therefore been carried out in close coordination with the preparation of the societal security report, "Social Security in an Uncertain World", which provides a more detailed account of developments in civilian sectors

[3944] Appendix 1 The Chief of Defence's comments on the government's recommendation on the further development of the Armed Forces

[3945] Introduction The Chief of Defence's expert military council A strengthened defence was presented on 8 October 2019, describing four comprehensive and scalable options that responded to different operational and financial ambition levels

[3946] The council relied on the mandate from the government of April 5 of the same year

[3947] The following aspects were emphasized

[3948] – The security situation is more serious and the possible threats more challenging than before

[3949] Norway should take greater responsibility in our immediate areas and contribute more to NATO's collective defense

[3950] – Norway should move further towards the goal of spending 2% of GDP on Defense

[3951] The professional military council sought to respond to challenges within the following areas

[3952] – Increased demands for military presence in our surrounding areas

[3953] – Increased demands for contributions to NATO's force structure and operations

[3954] – Greater needs related to the requirements for national contributions when receiving allied reinforcements

[3955] The Government's recommendation in this long-term plan involves continued prioritization and strengthening of the Armed Forces

[3956] However, some challenges remain

[3957] Individual capabilities and strengthening of staffing are coming later than recommended from a professional military standpoint

[3958] The long-term plan gives me good opportunities to develop and strengthen the Armed Forces if we are successful in implementing it

[3959] I will take overall responsibility for implementing and carrying out the plan

[3960] Filling the strength structure is important early in the period

[3961] I want to further develop the practice of conscription so that it becomes more flexible than it is today

[3962] Together with further investment in reservists, this provides good opportunities for building a more robust force structure in the Armed Forces

[3963] Preparedness and responsiveness are key concepts in a strengthened defense

[3964] Within the framework provided by this long-term plan, I would like to emphasize that the Armed Forces are organized and operate as uniformly as possible in peace, crisis and war

[3965] The long-term plan emphasizes the importance of collaboration; internally in the defense sector, through continued development of total defense and cooperation with close allies

[3966] Further development of cooperation will be an important task going forward

[3967] In order to reduce vulnerability, preserve our own freedom of action and ability to receive allied airstrikes, there is a need for an earlier strengthening of air defense than is included in the long-term plan

[3968] Furthermore, an earlier introduction of ground-based long-range precision weapons would have contributed to increasing the Army's preparedness and response capability, especially in the northernmost areas

[3969] The work of investigating future maritime capacities to replace current platforms will be an important basis for future investments in operational capacities in the maritime domain

[3970] Efficiency The government's recommendation sets goals for the development of the Armed Forces, including efficiency requirements

[3971] Efficiency is crucial to ensuring that the Armed Forces use resources correctly at all times

[3972] The goal is to seek further efficiency improvements that can be translated into increased operational capability

[3973] I consider the government's goal to be ambitious, but entirely possible to realize in the sector

[3974] Conclusion Norway is facing a more demanding security situation

[3975] Increased demands from NATO for military force contributions to preparedness and operations are challenging the overall capacity of the Armed Forces

[3976] The Government's recommendation for the long-term plan for the Armed Forces responds to key requirements from NATO and entails a significant and necessary financial boost for the Armed Forces

[3977] With this plan, the Armed Forces will have an increased ability to meet security policy challenges compared to the current level

[3978] However, the development of some capabilities and increased manning will come later than recommended from a professional military perspective
